plain_text.visual: Navy + white. Left: pile of books crossed out. Right: Bookster UI with completed reads. Bold headline overlay.
plain_text.concept: Comparison static. Contrast layout: unread stack vs. Bookster app. Before/After visual.
plain_text.primary: You already know which books matter. Bookster gets you through them — key ideas, 15 minutes, actually retained. Start free.
plain_text.headline: Read smarter, not longer.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rational tone + benefit hook for Achievers at mid-funnel produces higher-quality install than generic efficiency copy.
plain_text.learning_question: Does HK_Benefit outperform HK_Problem for a rational, ambitious avatar? ↘ diagonal ST_MOFU.

plain_text.visual: Aspirational palette — rich navy or forest green, warm gold accent. Clean desk setup or curated bookshelf. Feels premium.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle outcome static. Identity-upgrade framing. Not "save time" but "become the person who has read the things that matter."
plain_text.primary: The founders, operators, and professionals who stay sharp share one habit: they actually finish the books. Bookster makes that possible. Start free.
plain_text.headline: The reading list of people who stay ahead.
plain_text.hypothesis: Aspirational tone with problem hook creates tension for Achievers — they recognize the problem but feel pulled forward by aspiration.
plain_text.learning_question: Does TN_Aspirational + HK_Problem outperform TN_Rational + HK_Benefit (C1A) for the Achiever avatar?

plain_text.visual: High-contrast. Dark or navy background, white text. App rating visible (4.8★). Bookster logo prominent. CTA implied in layout hierarchy.
plain_text.concept: Comparison static pushed to maximum directness. Bottom-funnel — reader may have already seen Bookster. Short, no-introduction copy.
plain_text.primary: 15 minutes. Core ideas. Retained. Over 1,000 titles. Start your free trial — no card required.
plain_text.headline: Most book apps summarize. Bookster teaches.
plain_text.hypothesis: BOFU assertive comparison for solution-aware Achievers converts the comparison shopper with a direct final push.
plain_text.learning_question: Does ST_BOFU + TN_Assertive produce higher CVR for solution-aware Achievers vs MOFU content?

plain_text.visual: Bold, high-contrast. Dark background. Strong typographic hierarchy. Headline IS the visual. Data element (4M users) as graphic stat.
plain_text.concept: Behavior shift static. Confrontational but not hostile. Names the gap between aspiration and reality directly. ↙ diagonal PR_DataDriven.
plain_text.primary: It's not going to happen the way you've been trying. 4 million people changed their approach. 15 minutes a day. Start free.
plain_text.headline: You said you'd read more this year.
plain_text.hypothesis: Hardest combination: PAS + Assertive + Problem hook for Achievers. Tests whether maximum directness converts or repels the ambitious professional.
plain_text.learning_question: Is assertive PAS too aggressive for Achievers, or does the directness cut through where softer tones cannot? ↙ diagonal test.

plain_text.visual: Editorial palette — warm cream, deep green accent. Non-fiction books or podcast headphones. Overlay text structured, clean.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle static. Not a product demo — shows the reader you become. Editorial feel.
plain_text.primary: Most content disappears within 24 hours. Bookster turns 15 minutes into ideas you actually keep. Try it free.
plain_text.headline: You consume a lot. You retain less than you think.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rational tone creates cognitive dissonance for a depth-seeking aspirational avatar — logical framing where they expect emotional.
plain_text.learning_question: Can TN_Rational work for an identity-driven avatar, or does it flatten the message?

plain_text.visual: App screenshot dominant. Real Bookster library: philosophy shelf, economics shelf, history shelf — real titles visible. Headline overlaid above.
plain_text.concept: Product demo static. App library screenshot showing real book titles across philosophy, history, economics. The breadth IS the proof.
plain_text.primary: Bookster covers the books that matter — philosophy, history, economics, business, science. Read or listen. Key ideas retained. Try free today.
plain_text.headline: 1,000 books. 15 minutes each. Actually understand them.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rebuilt product demo with rational tone and problem hook converts deeper-learning audiences who need to see the product before committing. ↘ diagonal.
plain_text.learning_question: Does showing the real product (CN_ProductDemo) outperform lifestyle framing (C2A) for Depth Seekers?

plain_text.visual: Editorial. Rich, warm palette. Bookster library titles from philosophy and history — real, recognizable titles. Feels like a high-quality curated library.
plain_text.concept: Comparison static. Not cost comparison — quality comparison. Bookster vs skimming content and retaining nothing.
plain_text.primary: Over 1,000 titles spanning philosophy, history, economics, and science — condensed into 15-minute reads that hold the actual ideas. Start learning free.
plain_text.headline: Finally understand the books that matter.
plain_text.hypothesis: Aspirational tone with data proof — aspiration provides identity pull while data validates content quality. ↙ diagonal PR_DataDriven.
plain_text.learning_question: Can PR_DataDriven be aspirationally framed? Does data feel credible or cold for an identity-driven audience?

plain_text.visual: Aspirational editorial. Warm, rich palette. Books, knowledge, intellectual environment. Person implied — curious, engaged. No guilt, no missed deadlines.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle static. PAS reframed: the problem is not failure — it's untapped capability. Aspirational agitation.
plain_text.primary: The ideas in the books you haven't gotten to yet are still waiting. Bookster closes that gap. 15 minutes. Try free.
plain_text.headline: You're capable of understanding more than you've read.
plain_text.hypothesis: Most unexpected combination: PAS + Aspirational + Benefit hook. Tests whether intellectual aspiration can be agitated effectively.
plain_text.learning_question: Can FW_PAS be aspirationally toned? Does agitating a desire (rather than a pain) work as persuasion?

plain_text.visual: Clean, minimal. White background. Typography-forward. Stat overlay: "80% of books go unfinished." Deliberately rational visual register.
plain_text.concept: Behavior shift static. Names the behavioral pattern as a logical sequence. Rational register throughout.
plain_text.primary: Most books lose 80% of readers before chapter 3. The format is the problem — not you. Bookster works differently. Try free.
plain_text.headline: You start books. You don't finish them. There's a reason.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rational tone applied to a naturally emotional avatar tests whether logical or empathetic framing is the correct register for C3.
plain_text.learning_question: Does TN_Rational land for Foggy Brain, or does it feel tone-deaf? Key C3 diagnostic.

plain_text.visual: Warm, calm palette — soft cream or warm white. Open book with bookmark stuck in chapter 1. Feels relatable, not clinical.
plain_text.concept: Behavior shift static. Recognition-first creative. Names the experience without naming any condition. PAS + Emotional register.
plain_text.primary: Most people with a stack of unread books aren't lazy — they're stuck with a format that wasn't built for them. 4 million people switched to Bookster. Try it free.
plain_text.headline: You've started that book three times.
plain_text.hypothesis: Core C3 formula. PAS + Emotional + Problem hook. ↙ diagonal tests whether data proof (PR_DataDriven) adds or subtracts from the emotional register.
plain_text.learning_question: Does adding PR_DataDriven to an emotional PAS message lift or dampen conversion for empathy-first audiences?

plain_text.visual: Softest visual in the matrix. Warm cream background. Person reading comfortably — relaxed, enjoying it. Small Bookster UI inset. Natural light.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle static. Not comparison, not demo — identity of the learner who found their way in. Warm, inviting, no shame. ↘ diagonal ST_MOFU.
plain_text.primary: Short, structured, no 300-page commitment. Bookster works the way your brain does. Try it free — no pressure, no guilt.
plain_text.headline: Reading that actually fits how you think.
plain_text.hypothesis: Lifestyle + benefit hook for Foggy Brain tests whether leading with the positive outcome converts better than the problem frame.
plain_text.learning_question: Does HK_Benefit outperform HK_Problem for C3? Does framing around gain (ease, fit, relief) outperform guilt/friction?

plain_text.visual: Warmest visual in the matrix. Soft, inviting. Person mid-read, relaxed, comfortable. Warm lighting. Headline feels like something a friend would say.
plain_text.concept: Behavior shift static. Full empathy mode. Names the start-and-stall experience. Validates without judgment. Most emotionally resonant cell in the matrix.
plain_text.primary: Reading isn't the problem. Most books just weren't designed for how you actually think. Bookster was. Try it free — no long books, no guilt.
plain_text.headline: You've started that book three times. It's okay.
plain_text.hypothesis: The full empathy formula for Foggy Brain: PAS + Emotional + Problem hook. The highest-potential C3 cell.
plain_text.learning_question: Does the full empathy PAS outperform TN_Rational (C3A) and HK_Benefit (C3C) for the Foggy Brain avatar?

plain_text.visual: Clean white. Two-column: LEFT — physical book with price tag. RIGHT — Bookster app with price. Numbers are the visual hero.
plain_text.concept: Comparison static. Cost-focused. Before: book costs + unfinished reads. After: Bookster value. Bridge: clear cost comparison.
plain_text.primary: You've spent over $200 on books this year. Bookster gives you 1,000+ titles for less than a coffee a month. And you'll actually finish them. Try free.
plain_text.headline: $18 a book. $9 a month for all of them.
plain_text.hypothesis: Confirmed control formula. Replicates Pauli H2 commercial signal in U.S. English static format. ↙ diagonal PR_DataDriven.
plain_text.learning_question: Does this replicate the only confirmed purchase signal in U.S. English? Baseline for all other cells.

plain_text.visual: Same clean white comparison structure as C4A but typography bolder, larger. Primary headline is the visual hero. Less visual complexity.
plain_text.concept: Comparison static. Same comparison frame as C4A but with direct, confident, no-hedging assertive voice. No data required — assertion carries authority.
plain_text.primary: You know which ones they are. Bookster gives you the ideas without the shelf guilt. Less than a coffee a month. Start free.
plain_text.headline: Stop buying books you won't finish.
plain_text.hypothesis: Assertive tone for Growth Woman tests whether a harder register outperforms the warmer rational approach (C4A). Isolates TN_Assertive vs TN_Rational.
plain_text.learning_question: Does TN_Assertive produce better performance than TN_Rational for the same avatar and concept structure?

plain_text.visual: Clean, structured, conversion-optimized. White background. Bookster interface showing book count or category breadth. Headline bold, direct.
plain_text.concept: Comparison static at BOFU pressure. Rational, direct, minimal. The reader already knows they should do this — the ad removes the final objection.
plain_text.primary: 1,000+ titles. 15 minutes each. Less than a coffee a month. Your free trial starts today — no card required.
plain_text.headline: The books you want to read. Actually finished.

plain_text.visual: Clean rational comparison. Cost data prominent: "$300/year on books, finishes fewer than 5" as graphic stat. Bookster as smarter alternative.

conversion_tracking_signal.note: Conversion-based tracking: funnel actions are attributed to the converting device/platform/placement. Spend and impressions are not device-attributable under this tracking, so no CPA/CTR exist here. The export window may differ from the account's campaign window — treat cross-surface comparisons as directional.

message_pillars.label: Personal story made physical
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Turn a street into the protagonist of the recipient's life story. The gift lands because the place means something — the emotional core of the brand and the source of the account's best purchase-per-dollar signal.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Pillar ads ('1 Print Static', '2 Print Static', '2 Print + Dads Gift'): $141.69 spend, 4,254 impressions, 1 of 2 account purchases. The converting ad alone: $107.24, 3,160 impressions, CPA $107.24 — vs $364.86 / 0 purchases on the discount grid. Validation_required (single purchase, mixed attribution).
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU cold gift seekers; occasion overlays (Father's Day, anniversary, housewarming) are cycle-2 extensions of this pillar.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Static, warm lifestyle photography, single print staged in a domestic scene, precisely-named street visible in the artwork, short copy (2-4 lines), recipient-reaction narrative, implicit personalization CTA ('Find his city'). Single copy variant per test cell — copy fragmentation (15-29 variants/ad) destroyed isolation in the historical window.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Directional only — conversion-based device export (2026-01-01 → 2026-07-09, wider than the demo window): link clicks skew 94.5% mobile (iphone 932 + android 211 + tablets 83 of 1,298); Feed carries 941 link clicks; the account's single tracked-checkout purchase path ran through Instagram Stories. No placement spend/impressions exist under conversion tracking, so no placement CPA/CTR — run broad placements; treat these splits as delivery hints, not performance reads.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Scale-test candidate per analysis_core, but nothing scales from this window: validate through MST cycle 1 (gift-moment 3x3) first. No cell above 5% of budget for unproven variants.

message_pillars.label: Gallery quality, not a poster
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Neutralize the 'is this just a cheap poster?' objection with spec proof: heavyweight fine-art paper, archival inks, real wood frames, guarantee.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: 'Good quality ad' (retargeting): $127.33, 3,286 impressions, 0 purchases. Analysis_core flags the retargeting pool size as unverified — the read is 'optimize after pool-size check', not 'failed'. Validation_required.
message_pillars.funnel_application: BOFU retargeting — objection rebuttal for browsers who didn't buy.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Macro product close-up (frame corner, paper texture), 'not a poster' spec language, guarantee + free shipping reassurance, dark-macro design system.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Unknown — placement metrics unavailable in this window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: 25% of budget to BOFU quality-rebuttal retargeting AFTER the pool-size check, per budget guidance. Do not scale prospecting with this pillar.

message_pillars.label: 3,000 cities, breadth and choice
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Any place that matters is printable — hometown, college town, honeymoon coast. Breadth is the rational proof that the buyer's specific place exists in the catalog.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Pillar splits cleanly in the data: authentic spread ('Multiple Pieces' + '6 Images') $255.03, 15,174 impressions, 1 purchase (CPA $172.38 on the converting ad) — while the 25%-off catalog grid ('9 Image + Discount') burned $364.86 / 11,797 impressions / 0 purchases. Breadth converts when proven authentically, not via discount overlay. Validation_required.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU/MOFU solution-aware browsers; the authentic-spread execution carries the pillar, the discount-grid execution is quarantined.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Real (non-mockup) photo of 5-9 framed prints leaned on furniture, catalog-breadth copy ('cities, coasts, and countries'), craftsmanship cues ('museum-quality paper'), NO discount overlay.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Unknown — placement metrics unavailable in this window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Part of the 60% validate allocation: A/B real-photo spread vs catalog-grid mockup at equal budget, no discount in either arm. Hold discount executions at ≤15% of budget pending attribution reconciliation.

message_pillars.label: City identity pride
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Sell the city as identity — neighborhood name-stacking flatters the local and makes the print a badge of belonging.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: 'Music Row Static - Pride' $233.55 / 6,476 impressions and 'Blue Shirt UGC' $53.73 / 1,102 impressions — $287.28 combined, 0 reported purchases across static and UGC formats. Untested geo-tight; do not judge the concept on broad delivery. Validation_required.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU, geo-targeted only. Broad delivery wastes the geo-specific flattery (LD-H3).
message_pillars.execution_specifications: One city per creative, neighborhood name-stack ('Music Row. Lower Broad. East Nash.'), local-identity call-out headline, lifestyle mockup or UGC talking-head format.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Unknown — placement metrics unavailable in this window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Zero MST-cycle-1 budget. Geo-tight Nashville re-test as a separate experiment before any further spend against this pillar.

message_pillars.label: Social proof and reviews
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Let customers sell it — verbatim testimonial quotes and review-count trust bars ('4.9, 450+ reviews') as the proof layer for hesitant buyers.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: '1 Image Static - Best Sellers' (verbatim customer quote): $149.59, 6,707 impressions, 0 purchases. '2 Print + Dads Gift' (stat-question social proof): $11.62, 387 impressions, 0 purchases — below any read threshold. Validation_required.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU/MOFU — testimonial creative doubles as cold-traffic story and mid-funnel reassurance.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: First-person verbatim customer quote as primary text, single print in styled interior, or stat-question hook ('100 dads already have one. Does yours?') with review trust bar.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Unknown — placement metrics unavailable in this window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Test allocation only. Use as the proof row in MST cells rather than a standalone scaling pillar until a purchase signal exists.

active_hypotheses.label: Two buyer paths exist: young gift buyers (25-34) respond to recipient-story creative; 55+ self-decorators respond to authentic product spreads. Messaging should split by ICP.

icp_profiles.profile_name: Young Adult Gift Buyer (buying FOR parent/partner)
icp_profiles.message_resonance: Emotional gift narrative (LD-CN-GIFT-MOMENT). The converting ad spent $107.24 total — the account's best purchase-per-dollar signal.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: Converted on HK_Story + HK_Shock hook ('made a grown man cry' lineage) with a precisely-named street in the artwork. Zero purchases from this segment on catalog/offer creative despite broader delivery.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU — cold, problem-aware gift seekers around gifting moments (Father's Day window in the data).
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: Shopping for an emotionally meaningful, non-generic gift for a parent or partner. Responds to recipient-reaction narratives ('watch their face light up'), not product specs or discounts. Gift anxiety — wants the gift to land, fears giving something forgettable.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Male 25-34 — the account's 8th-largest segment ($123.70 spend, 6,835 impressions) yet it produced 1 of the 2 account purchases (2026-06-21, on the gift-narrative creative '1 Print Static'). Buyer is not the recipient: the purchase creative is written entirely about someone else's street.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Primary ICP for MST cycle 1. Run gift-narrative cells broad and let delivery re-find younger gift buyers; do not hard-restrict age yet (delivery skew currently sends 52% of spend to 55+).

icp_profiles.message_resonance: Authentic product spread (LD-CN-PRODUCT-SPREAD) — real photo, no overlay, no discount. Secondary winning-stack hypothesis from analysis_core.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: Converted on PR_Demonstration (real photo of framed prints leaned on furniture) with rational catalog-breadth copy. Zero purchases from the same segments on the 25%-off catalog grid ($364.86, 0 purchases account-wide).
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU/MOFU — solution-aware browsers; testimonial and quality-proof creative are natural MOFU/BOFU follow-ups for this ICP.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: Decorating their own home with meaningful places — cities of first trips, honeymoons, hometowns. Values perceived craftsmanship ('museum-quality paper', real wood frames) and authenticity; a real unstyled photo outperformed the polished discount grid for this segment.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: 55+ segments absorbed $851.70 (51.6% of account spend, ~24,400 impressions) and produced 1 purchase: female 55-64 on 'Multiple Pieces' (2026-05-06) — an authentic multi-print product spread with no discount overlay.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Secondary ICP for MST cycle 1. A/B real-photo spread vs catalog-grid mockup at equal budget with NO discount in either arm, per the analysis_core next-sprint recommendation.

icp_profiles.message_resonance: Unproven. City-pride creative must be re-tested geo-tight before the concept is judged.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: None validated. Analysis_core flags that broad (non-geo-targeted) delivery likely wasted the geo-specific message — the concept is untested, not disproven.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU — geo-targeted cold audiences in the named city only.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: Identity-driven local — buys the city as a badge ('NASHVILLE ART for a NASHVILLE LOVER'). Neighborhood name-stacking (Music Row, 12 South, Belle Meade) is the flattery mechanic.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: No converting segment yet. The two city-pride creatives ('Music Row Static - Pride' static + 'Blue Shirt UGC') spent $287.28 across 7,578 impressions with 0 reported purchases.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Hold out of MST cycle 1 budget. Run a separate geo-tight Nashville test before spending against this ICP again — do not kill on 0 purchases until attribution is reconciled.

testing_framework.matrix_position: Full 3x3 gift-moment MST (cycle 1) — hook axis x concept-staging axis, single copy variant per cell
testing_framework.success_criteria: Any cell CPA below the $107.24 historical benchmark at reconciled attribution; >= 30 purchases per read window before scale/kill calls
testing_framework.isolated_variable: Hook type (HK_Story/Shock vs HK_Question vs HK_Stat) x concept staging (kitchen gift scene vs unwrap moment vs recipient reaction). Copy architecture, design system, CTA and street-name personalization held constant across all 9 cells.
testing_framework.learning_objective: Which hook x staging combination carries the gift-moment narrative — and does Advantage+ re-find 25-34 gift buyers when creative speaks to them (52% of historical spend skewed 55+)?
testing_framework.matrix_naming_convention: LD_GIFT_{HOOK}_{STAGING}_001 — hooks: STORY (Story/Shock), QUESTION, STAT; stagings: KITCHEN (kitchen gift scene), UNWRAP (unwrap moment), REACTION (recipient reaction)

performance_tracking.timeline: 14-day read windows; evaluate only after attribution reconciliation against server-side purchase counts

decision_rules.kill_if: No cell produces a purchase at 2x benchmark spend — fall back to the product-spread lane (LD-H2) as primary direction
decision_rules.scale_if: Cell produces purchases below the $107.24 benchmark CPA at >= 30 reconciled purchases
decision_rules.iterate_if: Purchase signal exists but above benchmark — iterate staging within the winning hook column

performance_tracking.budget_allocation: Within the 60% validate allocation; no cell above 5% of account budget per IAP validate rules
performance_tracking.campaign_structure: Single MST campaign, 9 ad sets (one per cell), broad delivery, standard attribution

Isolated variables (hook, staging) clearly executed; all other elements match across cells

executive_summary.verdict: INVALID TEST — do not action. Spend ($57.97) is 5.8% of the committed pilot budget, zero purchases or checkouts were recorded across an 11-day window, and 4 of 16 matrix cells never delivered at all. The blocking issues are operational (tracking + delivery), not creative or audience quality, and must be fixed before this sprint can produce a usable read on avatar, PMF, or variable-stack performance.
executive_summary.avatar_pmf_read: Not evaluable this cycle. All four ICPs (GiftGiver45, Milestone2534, HometownSelf, MemoryKeeperCouple) have at least one cell with zero delivery, so no avatar can be fairly compared to the others yet. The one persistent signal worth carrying forward: recorded spend still skews ~66% toward the 45+ segment, which was the exact problem the pre-pilot CBO/targeting fix was meant to solve — worth a direct look at current campaign-level targeting settings, independent of the MST creative read.
executive_summary.communications_read: Not evaluable — no conversion signal exists to judge message-market fit of any headline, hook, or proof treatment. The only directional (non-verdict) click signal: C3A ("Look closer. Those are real street names.", 5.3% link CTR on 151 impressions) and C1B ("What do you give someone who has everything?", 2.1% CTR) are the only cells with any above-baseline engagement — noted for visibility, explicitly not a basis for action.
executive_summary.variable_stack_read: Not evaluable — see winning_variable_stack. All prior hypotheses (row isolation, diagonal reads) remain hypotheses; none can be promoted or retired on this data.
executive_summary.audience_performance_read: Reach and impressions concentrate in the 45-54 and 55-64 male segments; ~66% of the $57.97 recorded spend sits in 45+ across genders. Traffic volume overall is too low (1,951 impressions, 23-341 link clicks depending on which export you trust) for any audience-segment conversion comparison.

performance_tiers.note: No cell has enough spend or conversion volume to support a tier assignment per the tiering criteria (which require ROAS and buying-intent signal). insight_confidence.what_would_change_this: Resolve the Initiate Checkout tracking gap, get all 16 cells delivering, and accumulate real spend against the ~$1,000 committed budget before re-running this analysis.

message_pillars.label: Free-Access Aspiration — Career Reinvention via Low-Barrier Entry
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Capture high-intent career-transition seekers at TOFU with 'free' and 'training' access framing, which consistently delivers the lowest cost per result in the lead_gen objective across the account. The evidence is unambiguous: FREE ($1.62–$4.65 CPA across multiple ad variants), FREETRAINING ($2.12–$2.13 CPA), DREAMCAREER ($1.64 CPA), and ESCAPE ($1.62–$1.75 CPA) all dramatically outperform commitment-implying language like ENROLL ($7.19 CPA equivalent in city-token cluster) or income-number claims. Static image format (STAT_ system) is the primary discovery vehicle for this ICP. The goal of this pillar is to isolate which aspirational angle — benefit-led dream outcome vs. pain-led escape — maximizes lead_gen volume at the lowest cost per qualified lead.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: DREAMCAREER token: 1,200 results, CPA $1.64, CVR 39.4% (56–63 unique ads). FREETRAINING token: 661 results, CPA $2.12, CVR 53.9% (148 unique ads). ESCAPE token: 656 results, CPA $1.62, CVR 42.8% (67 unique ads). FREE token: 959 results, CPA $3.78 across broader set but STAT_FREE_04.jpg delivers CPA $1.67, CVR 52.4%; STAT_ESCAPE_10.jpg delivers CPA $1.64, CVR 39.2%; STAT_ESCAPE_04.jpg delivers CPA $1.75, CVR 45.4%. STOPCHASING (anti-motivation framing): CPA $3.76–$5.14, CVR 51.4–55.4% — higher CPA despite competitive CVR, suggesting weaker hook-to-offer alignment. 8.4 gen.mp4 (video, lead_gen): CPA $1.88, CVR 49.2%, 327–654 results — the only video format competitive with static for this objective. STAT_FREETRAINING_01.jpg: CPA $1.80, CVR 56.5%, 271 results. All cost per result figures are for the lead_gen objective (cost per qualified lead).
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU entry via Facebook Feed and Instagram Feed static image ads under Advantage+ broad targeting. This ICP is AW_ProblemAware to AW_SolutionAware — content should affirm the possibility of change without requiring prior knowledge of the specific program. CTA family: 'Get Free Access', 'Start Free', 'Claim Your Spot' — avoid 'Enroll Now' or any payment-implying language.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Column C1 in the Matrix Sprint Test. Hold STAT_ static image design system and 'free access' CTA family constant across all four C1 cells. Row variable: hook type (HK_Problem in C1A, HK_Benefit in C1B, HK_Curiosity in C1C, HK_SocialProof in C1D). All other angle variables must differ across rows. Creative naming anchors: use ESCAPE/DREAMCAREER/FREETRAINING vocabulary in copy. Do NOT use city-specific overlays — broad Advantage+ targeting is more efficient for this ICP. Include one video cell (replicating 8.4 gen.mp4 format) as a format variable isolated in a diagonal position.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements with broad targeting. Facebook Feed ($4.39 CPA, 1,503 results) and Instagram Feed ($5.08 CPA, 1,082 results) are primary volume drivers at the account level. Do not manually exclude placements — allow algorithm to optimize. Static image assets will auto-adapt to Stories and Reels placements where eligible.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: ABO budgeting. This is the highest-confidence pillar — DREAMCAREER and ESCAPE creatives are already below $2.00 cost per qualified lead with meaningful result volume. Once the matrix identifies the winning hook variable (expected: HK_Benefit based on directional STOPCHASING underperformance), consolidate spend behind winning cell and expand to a follow-on BAB framework test.

message_pillars.label: Treatment-Specific Visual Proof — Aesthetic Outcome Credibility
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Convert aesthetics-interested women aged 35–54 who are already solution-aware by leading with named treatment outcomes and clinical visual proof rather than generic beauty messaging. The evidence shows that specificity in treatment naming (FIXFROWNLINES, PERFECTPOUT, PEPTIDE) reliably delivers CPA $1.28–$2.35 for the lead_gen objective, while generic or free-filler framing underperforms. This pillar tests whether copy framework (how the outcome is framed — transformation arc vs. direct outcome statement vs. pain agitation) is the variable that determines which specific treatment angle scales further. This is a lead_gen objective pillar; all cost metrics refer to cost per qualified lead.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: PERFECTPOUT token: 451 results, CPA $2.29, CVR 58.5% (67 unique ads). STAT_PERFECTPOUT_07.jpg: CPA $1.82, CVR 64.7%, 55 results. STAT_PERFECTPOUT_04.jpg: CPA $1.50, CVR 65.5%, 55 results. FIXFROWNLINES token: 594 results, CPA $2.97, CVR 56.8% (46 unique ads). STAT_FIXFROWNLINES_01.jpg: CPA $2.23, CVR 59.1%, 274 results. PEPTIDE token: 398 results, CPA $1.97, CVR 61.9% (45 unique ads). STAT_PEPTIDE_09.jpg: CPA $2.13, CVR 59.8%, 119 results. FREEFILLER token (free-framing variant): CPA $3.74, CVR 45.6%, 73 results — underperforms named treatment ads by 25–59% on CPA, suggesting 'free' framing weakens intent quality for this ICP. ChatGPT Image Jul 31 PNG: CPA $1.28, CVR 64.6%, 720 results — the highest-volume, lowest-CPA lead_gen ad in the account; likely an aesthetic visual given the design-tool origin. Demographic anchor: female 45–54 and female 35–44 are the only purchase-converting segments in the account (CPA $33.42 and $36.95 respectively on ecommerce purchases, sourced from the demographic report at 95.7% spend coverage).
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU entry — this ICP is already solution-aware and evaluating specific providers. Ads should lead with the named outcome (e.g., 'eliminate frown lines', 'perfect pout') and a clinical or social proof element. CTA family: 'Book Your Consultation', 'See Results', 'Learn More' — avoid 'FREE' framing based on FREEFILLER underperformance evidence. Follow-on retargeting should introduce PR_Expert (injector credentials or clinical setting visual).
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Column C3 in the Matrix Sprint Test. Hold treatment-specific visual design system (clinical, clean aesthetic) and consultation-framing CTA constant across all four C3 cells. Row variable: FW_ copy framework (FW_FAB in C3A as control replication, FW_BAB in C3B, FW_PAS in C3C, FW_Direct in C3D). Treatment subject should rotate across rows (lip, frown, peptide, new treatment) to prevent row-constant confounding. PR_ proof type must vary independently of FW_ within each row.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements, broad targeting. Facebook Feed and Instagram Feed are primary for this ICP based on the demographic purchase-conversion concentration in female 35–54. Instagram Explore Home shows a directional low CPA ($1.30 across 2 results — thin evidence, below the threshold for confidence) but should not be manually targeted; allow Advantage+ to discover it organically.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: ABO budgeting. Moderate scaling confidence — PERFECTPOUT and PEPTIDE are proven at the ad level but FW_ framework has not been isolated. Do not scale until the matrix identifies a winning framework. Watch cost per qualified lead vs. cost per purchase lag — the ecommerce terminal metric requires downstream purchase attribution which is currently sparse in the demographic data (10–11 female purchase conversions visible). Do not conflate lead volume with purchase performance.

message_pillars.label: AI-Native Static Imagery — Format Efficiency Hypothesis
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: The top-performing ad in the account by CPA and CVR is an AI-generated static image (ChatGPT Image Jul 31, 2026, CPA $1.28, CVR 64.6%, 1,440 results). This pillar isolates whether the image generation method (AI-native visual style) is itself a causal driver of performance, or whether the result is attributable to the specific offer/copy pairing. If AI-generated imagery consistently outperforms photographer-sourced STAT_ imagery at equivalent offer and copy, it justifies a systematic shift in creative production methodology. Secondary test: whether AI-generated imagery scales across both the career-transition and aesthetic ICPs or is ICP-specific. This is a cross-objective hypothesis pillar — evidence spans both lead_gen and unknown result types; do not collapse into a single cost per result.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: ChatGPT Image Jul 31, 2026, 03_22_35 PM.png (lead_gen): CPA $1.28, CVR 64.6%, 720 results, spend $919.16, impressions 49,004, CTR 2.28% — the single highest-CVR and lowest-CPA ad with meaningful volume in the account. Image Aug 4, 2026, 03_53_02 PM.png (lead_gen): CPA $2.52, CVR 40.3%, 79 results, spend $199.33 — a second AI-generated image, lower CVR but still competitive. By contrast, top STAT_ performer STAT_FREETRAINING_01.jpg: CPA $1.80, CVR 56.5%, 271 results; STAT_FREE_04.jpg: CPA $1.67, CVR 52.4%, 155 results. The AI image outperforms the best STAT_ image by 29% on CPA and 14 percentage points on CVR, with 2.65x the result volume. This is a directional signal requiring isolation — the AI image may benefit from a stronger underlying offer rather than the visual format alone.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU discovery across both ICP columns. The AI-generated visual format should be tested in C1 (career ICP) and C3 (aesthetic ICP) diagonal positions so that if the format variable is isolated across different avatars, the matrix can determine whether it is universally superior or ICP-specific. Pair with the copy/hook frameworks already proven per ICP to avoid confounding format with copy.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: This pillar's variable (CN_UGC / AI-native image format) should appear in exactly 3–4 cells distributed across the matrix — specifically recommended for main diagonal positions (C1A, C2B, C3C) and one counter-diagonal position (C4A) to achieve cross-avatar isolation per IAP golden rule. Do not cluster all AI image tests in one column. In each cell, the copy framework and offer must match the adjacent STAT_ control cell in the same row to isolate the visual format variable cleanly.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements, broad targeting. The ChatGPT Image performed at CTR 2.28% on Facebook/Instagram Feed mix — above the account's Facebook Feed benchmark of 1.37% CTR. Allow algorithm to self-optimize placement; do not restrict to Feed only despite Feed being the dominant volume driver.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: ABO budgeting. This pillar carries medium confidence — the lead AI image has real volume (720 results, $919 spend) but the second AI image underperforms (79 results, CPA $2.52), suggesting the format is not uniformly superior. Run the matrix sprint before scaling. If 3 of 4 AI-format diagonal cells outperform their STAT_ row counterparts on cost per result, this becomes a primary creative production signal.

message_pillars.label: Professional Business-Builder Offer — Exploratory Validation Column
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: The LOUIS and DENTISTPROFIT creative cluster represents a distinct offer type — professional income augmentation for health-adjacent practitioners — but currently underperforms at CPA $6.52–$18.05 for lead_gen, 3–10x worse than STAT_ static benchmarks. This pillar does not assert that the ICP is viable; it tests whether the underperformance is caused by weak creative angles (income-number claims, city specificity) rather than a fundamentally unresponsive audience. The hypothesis is that replacing income-claim hooks with CN_FounderStory or CN_Expert framing and removing city overlays will bring CPA within 2x of the STAT_ benchmark. If no C4 cell achieves this threshold, the ICP is deprioritized for the next sprint. This is a lead_gen objective pillar (cost per qualified lead). Avatar basis: exploratory — no high-confidence demographic foundation exists for this segment in the evidence.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: LOUIS token (335–600 unique ads): 600 results, CPA $10.50, CVR 23.7% — materially worse than career and aesthetic segments. VID_LOUIS_10k_I.mp4 (income claim variant): CPA $17.47, CVR 21.8%, 34 results. VID_LOUIS_10k_O.mp4: CPA $18.05, CVR 13.2%, 32 results — worst performer in the LOUIS cluster. VID_LOUIS_NYC_IN.mp4: CPA $7.38, CVR 29.4%, 37 results — best in city-specific LOUIS set. VID_LOUIS_DAL_IN.mp4: CPA $8.12, CVR 33.75%, 27 results. STAT_DENTISTPROFIT_03.jpg: CPA $6.43, CVR 31.4%, 38 results. STAT_LV_INJECT_2.png: CPA $5.05, CVR 39.3%, 42 results — closest to account benchmark in this cluster. City-specific ad CPAs range $5.05–$18.05; removing the income-number claim and city overlay is the primary test variable. Note: this segment has no purchase-attributed demographic data and no concept_rollup data; all claims are grounded in raw token and ad-level rollup only. Confidence level: low for all performance claims here.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU only. This ICP likely requires a two-step funnel (awareness ad → retargeting with proof/case study) but the matrix sprint should establish whether any single-step entry is viable first. If C4 cells generate qualified leads at cost per result below 2x the STAT_ benchmark ($3.50 threshold), introduce a MOFU retargeting layer in the subsequent sprint.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Column C4 as exploratory expansion column. Avatar basis: exploratory; target ICP blank. Hold TN_Rational tone and FW_StoryBrand framework constant across all C4 cells. Row variable: CN_ concept angle (CN_FounderStory in C4A, CN_Expert in C4B, CN_Comparison in C4C, CN_Testimonial in C4D). Remove all income-number claims and city-specific overlays. No video in C4 — LOUIS video consistently underperforms static; test static-only for this column. CTA family: 'Learn How It Works', 'See the Opportunity' — avoid 'Enroll' or dollar-amount promises.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements, broad targeting. Minimum viable ABO budget only — do not allocate primary spend here until validation threshold is met. Facebook Feed is the likely primary placement given the professional audience profile, but do not manually restrict.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: ABO at minimum budget. Success threshold: at least 2 of 4 C4 cells must achieve cost per qualified lead below $7.00 (2x the $3.50 STAT_ benchmark) within the sprint window before any budget increase is considered. If threshold is not met, deprioritize this ICP and reallocate C4 budget to C1 or C3 in the following sprint.

active_hypotheses.label: Replacing anti-motivation 'STOPCHASING' hook framing with benefit-led 'DREAMCAREER' aspiration framing will reduce cost per qualified lead for the career-transition ICP by at least 30%, because the evidence shows DREAMCAREER delivers CPA $1.64 vs STOPCHASING CPA $3.76–$5.14 on near-equivalent CVR, suggesting hook polarity (positive aspiration vs. negative escape from bad outcome) is the performance driver rather than funnel stage or format.
active_hypotheses.source: STOPCHASING token ads (STAT_STOPCHASING_02.jpg: CPA $3.76, CVR 55.4%, 155 results)
active_hypotheses.risk: The DREAMCAREER vs STOPCHASING difference may reflect offer specificity or creative execution rather than hook polarity alone — the token names suggest different underlying copy, not just hook type. Isolation is imperfect given the raw_token evidence base. Confidence: medium.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: HK_Benefit hook with DREAMCAREER-equivalent positive aspiration copy, holding STAT_ static image format, FW_PAS framework, and 'free access' CTA constant. Place in C1B (row B = HK_Benefit shared variable) and replicate the hook in C2B and C3B to isolate it across two additional avatars simultaneously.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_ hook polarity: HK_Benefit (positive outcome aspiration) vs HK_Problem (negative escape / STOPCHASING framing). Distribution: HK_Benefit appears in row B across C1B, C2B, C3B, C4B (4 cells, different avatars and copy frameworks per cell) — exactly 4 appearances across varied contexts, satisfying the golden rule. HK_Problem appears in row A across all 4 columns as the control row. The diagonal will not carry HK_ as its shared variable, preserving it for CN_ or FW_ isolation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C1B achieves cost per qualified lead ≤ $2.30 (30% improvement over STOPCHASING control $3.76) within the sprint window with minimum 50 results. If all three HK_Benefit row cells (C1B, C2B, C3B) outperform their respective HK_Problem row counterparts (C1A, C2A, C3A) on cost per result, HK_Benefit is confirmed as a dominant variable for the next sprint.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High impact if confirmed — shifting the entire career-ICP creative library from problem-hook to benefit-hook framing could reduce blended cost per qualified lead by 20–40% based on directional evidence.

active_hypotheses.label: AI-generated static imagery (CN_UGC / ChatGPT Image visual style) will outperform photographer-sourced STAT_ static imagery on cost per result by at least 20% when copy framework and offer are held constant, because the ChatGPT Image Jul 31 PNG achieves CPA $1.28 and CVR 64.6% vs. the best STAT_ equivalent at CPA $1.67 and CVR 52.4% — a 23% CPA advantage and 12-point CVR advantage with meaningful spend ($919 vs $258).
active_hypotheses.source: STAT_FREE_04.jpg (CPA $1.67, CVR 52.4%, 155 results) as the best-matched STAT_ static control for offer and copy theme
active_hypotheses.risk: The ChatGPT Image Jul 31 advantage may be driven by the specific creative concept or copy rather than the AI-generated visual style. The second AI image (Aug 4, CPA $2.52) underperforms, suggesting the format is not uniformly superior. ABO spend may be insufficient to reach 30 results per cell in the sprint window if the exploratory columns (C4) dilute budget.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: AI-generated static image using the same copy theme and CTA as the control STAT_ ad, placed in main diagonal positions C1A, C2B, C3C and counter-diagonal position C4A. Each AI image cell is paired with a STAT_ image cell in the same row so direct format comparison is readable within the row.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: CN_ format production method: AI-generated image (CN_UGC proxy) vs. STAT_ static image. Distribution: AI-format appears in exactly 4 cells (C1A, C2B, C3C, C4A) across all four avatar columns and three different row contexts — satisfying the 2–4 appearance golden rule and achieving cross-avatar isolation via the diagonal. The matching STAT_ control format appears in the adjacent row cells (C1B, C2A, C3D, C4B). All other variables (copy framework, CTA, offer) held constant within each row pair.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: At least 3 of 4 AI-format diagonal cells achieve cost per result at least 15% lower than their STAT_ row-pair counterparts within the sprint window. Minimum 30 results per cell before verdict. Secondary signal: thumbstop / CTR comparison — AI image must show CTR ≥ 2.0% (vs. account Facebook Feed benchmark of 1.37%) to confirm the format is genuinely capturing attention rather than benefiting from a favorable offer assignment.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium impact — if confirmed, AI-generated imagery becomes the default static production method, reducing creative production cost and cycle time while maintaining or improving cost per result.

active_hypotheses.label: Replacing the FW_FAB copy framework with FW_BAB (Before-After-Bridge transformation narrative) for the aesthetic treatment ICP will reduce cost per qualified lead by at least 20%, because this audience is already solution-aware (AW_SolutionAware) and responds to outcome visualization — the BAB structure leads with the desired after-state before explaining the mechanism, matching their decision-making stage better than feature-advantage-benefit sequencing.
active_hypotheses.source: STAT_FIXFROWNLINES_01.jpg (CPA $2.23, CVR 59.1%, 274 results) as the FW_FAB control proxy for the aesthetic ICP
active_hypotheses.risk: FW_ framework isolation is confounded by the fact that treatment topic rotates across rows — frown line creative in row A may inherently differ from lip volume creative in row B independent of the framework. Mitigation: use the same treatment topic in C3A and C3B, varying only the framework.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: FW_BAB framework applied to the same treatment concept (frown line reduction or lip volume), holding CN_ProductDemo visual, TN_Warm tone, and consultation-framing CTA constant. Place in C3B. Replicate FW_BAB in C1B (career ICP) and C2B (exploratory ICP) to allow row-level isolation of FW_ variable across avatars.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: FW_ copy framework: FW_BAB (transformation narrative) vs FW_FAB (control). Distribution: FW_BAB appears in row B across C1B, C2B, C3B, C4B (4 cells) — different avatars, different design systems, same framework. FW_FAB appears in row A as the control row. FW_PAS and FW_Direct occupy rows C and D respectively. Each framework appears exactly 4 times across different avatar contexts, satisfying the golden rule. Note: FW_ framework has not been isolated in the existing evidence — this is a first-cycle isolation test. Confidence: low until matrix results are available.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C3B achieves cost per qualified lead ≤ $1.80 (20% improvement over $2.23 control) with minimum 40 results. If FW_BAB outperforms FW_FAB in at least 2 of 3 non-exploratory column cells (C1B, C2B, C3B), the framework is confirmed as the winner for the following sprint.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium impact — if FW_BAB is confirmed, it standardizes the copy architecture for the aesthetic ICP and potentially reduces creative briefing time. The performance delta may be smaller than the hook-polarity hypothesis given the already-high CVR of the control.

active_hypotheses.label: Removing income-number claims (e.g., '10K') and city-specific geographic overlays from the professional business-builder creative cluster will reduce cost per qualified lead in the exploratory C4 column by at least 40%, because the worst performers in the LOUIS cluster are those combining both variables (VID_LOUIS_10k_I.mp4: CPA $17.47; VID_LOUIS_10k_O.mp4: CPA $18.05), while the least-bad performers omit or soften the income claim (VID_LOUIS_NYC_IN.mp4: CPA $7.38; STAT_LV_INJECT_2.png: CPA $5.05).
active_hypotheses.source: VID_LOUIS_10k_I.mp4 (CPA $17.47, CVR 21.8%, 34 results) as the incumbent income-claim + city-specific control
active_hypotheses.risk: The underperformance of the LOUIS cluster may reflect a fundamentally unresponsive audience or a weak underlying offer rather than correctable creative variables. The evidence base for this segment is thin — STAT_LV_INJECT_2.png at CPA $5.05 is the only data point approaching the threshold, with only 42 results. High risk of wasted spend. Mitigation: minimum ABO budget only.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: CN_FounderStory static image ad with broad universal copy (no income number, no city name), FW_StoryBrand framework, TN_Rational tone, placed in C4A. Three additional C4 cells (C4B: CN_Expert, C4C: CN_Comparison, C4D: CN_Testimonial) test concept angle variation while all holding no-income-claim and no-city-overlay constant across the column.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HP_ pain framing + geographic specificity: removing income-number hooks and city overlays vs. including them. This is a two-variable change from the control, which is a limitation — strictly, only one variable should be isolated per cell. The pragmatic justification is that income-number and city overlay are always co-present in the worst performers and always absent in the least-bad performers, making it operationally reasonable to test their removal together as a bundle in the first cycle, then isolate them individually in a follow-on sprint if C4 shows improvement. Distribution: the no-claim, no-overlay format appears in all 4 C4 cells (constant column-level constraint, not a row variable). Concept angle (CN_) is the row variable for C4. Confidence: low — exploratory column with no demographic foundation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: At least 2 of 4 C4 cells achieve cost per qualified lead ≤ $7.00 (2x the $3.50 STAT_ benchmark) within the sprint window with minimum 20 results per cell. If threshold is not met by any C4 cell, the exploratory ICP is deprioritized and C4 budget is reallocated to C1 in the subsequent sprint.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Low-to-medium impact if validated — unlocking a professional B2B-adjacent lead segment would diversify the account's lead sources. However, the probability of validation within one sprint is low given current evidence.

active_hypotheses.label: Video format (8.4 gen.mp4 style) will not outperform AI-generated static imagery for the lead_gen objective in the career-transition ICP, and testing video vs. static within the same hook and framework will confirm static as the superior format for this objective, because the best static ad (ChatGPT Image Jul 31: CPA $1.28, CVR 64.6%) already outperforms the best video (8.4 gen.mp4: CPA $1.88, CVR 49.2%) by 32% on CPA and 15 points on CVR despite video having higher impression volume.
active_hypotheses.source: 8.4 gen.mp4 (CPA $1.88, CVR 49.2%, 327–654 results across two result-type splits) as the best-performing video format
active_hypotheses.risk: 8.4 gen.mp4's lower CVR relative to the ChatGPT Image may reflect the specific creative execution rather than the format — the video may have a weak hook or pacing issue unrelated to format type. Mitigation: use a new video creative with the same HK_Benefit hook and FW_PAS structure as the static control to minimize execution-level confounds.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: AI-generated static image holding identical offer, copy theme (free career training / dream career), and CTA as the 8.4 gen.mp4 control. Place in C1A (main diagonal, AI-format variable). The 8.4 gen.mp4 equivalent video format appears in C1C (row C = video format shared variable across columns) to enable direct within-column format comparison for the career ICP.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: CN_ format type: static image vs. short-form video. Distribution: video format appears in row C across C1C, C2C, C3C, C4C (4 cells, different avatars) — satisfying the golden rule of 2–4 appearances in varied contexts. Static image appears in rows A, B, D for C1. The comparison is readable at the column level (C1A static vs. C1C video, same ICP, same offer) and at the row level (C1C vs C2C vs C3C vs C4C, different ICPs, same format).
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C1A (AI static) achieves cost per qualified lead at least 15% lower than C1C (video) with minimum 50 results per cell. If the static advantage is confirmed in at least 2 of 3 non-exploratory column pairs (C1, C2, C3), static becomes the default format for lead_gen campaigns and video investment is redirected to brand awareness objectives.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium impact on production strategy — confirming static superiority for lead_gen would significantly reduce creative production cost and approval cycle time.

active_hypotheses.label: Treatment-specific CTAs ('Book Your Consultation', 'See Results') will outperform free-access CTAs ('Get Free Access', 'Claim Your Spot') for the aesthetic ICP on cost per qualified lead, because FREEFILLER token (CPA $3.74, CVR 45.6%) underperforms PERFECTPOUT (CPA $1.50–$2.29, CVR 57–65%) and PEPTIDE (CPA $1.97, CVR 61.9%), suggesting that 'free' framing reduces perceived treatment quality or provider credibility for this solution-aware audience.
active_hypotheses.source: STAT_FREEFILLER_02.jpg (CPA $3.74, CVR 45.6%, 73 results) as the free-framing CTA control for the aesthetic ICP
active_hypotheses.risk: The FREEFILLER vs PERFECTPOUT CPA difference may be driven by the treatment concept (filler is more commoditized than 'perfect pout') rather than the CTA language alone. Isolation is imperfect without a direct A/B swap of only the CTA on identical creative. This hypothesis should be treated as directional in the first sprint, with a dedicated CTA-only test in the follow-on sprint.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Identical treatment-specific visual and body copy as the FREEFILLER control ad, with only the CTA swapped to 'Book Your Free Consultation' (commitment-light but treatment-specific, not price-promise). Place in C3D as the FW_Direct row cell for the aesthetic column. A second variant using 'See Before & After Results' CTA appears in C2D to test the consultation-vs-proof CTA distinction across a second avatar.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: CTA family language: free-access framing vs. treatment-specific consultation framing. Distribution: treatment-specific CTA appears in C3D and C2D (2 cells, different avatars and design systems). Free-access CTA appears in C1D and C4D (2 cells, career and exploratory ICPs where it is contextually appropriate). Each CTA type appears exactly twice in varied contexts — satisfying the 2–4 golden rule minimum. Note: this is a CTA variable (column constant category in IAP), so its isolation across columns rather than rows is the appropriate axis.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C3D achieves cost per qualified lead ≤ $2.50 (33% improvement over FREEFILLER $3.74 control) with minimum 30 results. CVR should remain ≥ 55% (matching PERFECTPOUT benchmark) to confirm the consultation CTA maintains click quality rather than just improving downstream conversion.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium impact — confirming consultation-framing CTA superiority for the aesthetic ICP standardizes the CTA strategy and removes the risk of 'free' language undermining provider credibility for a treatment-seeking audience.

icp_profiles.profile_name: Facebook-Native Feed Converter — Mature Female, 45–54, Dual-Intent (Aesthetic + Career)
icp_profiles.message_resonance: Career angle: HK_Benefit + FW_PAS + TN_Aspirational + 'DREAMCAREER'/'ESCAPE'/'FREETRAINING' vocabulary at CPA $1.62–$2.12. Aesthetic angle: CN_ProductDemo + FW_FAB + TN_Warm + named treatment (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES, PEPTIDE) at CPA $1.50–$2.29. AI-generated static imagery directionally outperforms STAT_ photography (ChatGPT Image $1.28 vs best STAT_ $1.67). PR_VisualDemo and PR_Testimonial are hypothesized as higher-impact proof types for both angles, though not yet isolated. TN_Emotional and TN_Aspirational outperform TN_Urgent or anti-motivation framing (STOPCHASING CPA $3.76–$5.14 vs positive-frame equivalents $1.64–$2.12).
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: Engages with both static image and short-form video content, but static delivers dramatically lower cost per result across the account (CPA $1.28–$2.35 for top static ads vs. CPA $4.55–$17.86 for video equivalents). Facebook Feed is her primary discovery surface — the placement delivers 1.37% CTR at $4.39 CPA with 1,503 results, vs. Facebook Reels at 2.61% CTR but $8.78 CPA, suggesting she clicks thoughtfully rather than impulsively. CVR of 34–64% on link clicks across top performers indicates strong intent once attention is captured — the bottleneck is thumbstop, not post-click conviction. She is responsive to 'free' access framing for lead-gen offers (FREETRAINING, DREAMCAREER) but not for aesthetic treatment offers (FREEFILLER underperforms named treatment ads), suggesting her price sensitivity is category-specific. Urgency response: moderate; deadline or cohort framing may help but has not been isolated in the evidence.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: Facebook Feed at TOFU for career/training offers; Facebook Feed and Instagram Feed at MOFU for aesthetic treatment offers. She enters the career funnel via static image aspiration ads and the aesthetic funnel via treatment-specific visual proof ads. Instagram Stories ($7.19 CPA, 505 results) and Instagram Reels ($8.39 CPA, 348 results) are secondary placements — relevant for retargeting but not primary acquisition.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: This individual sits at the intersection of two strong motivational currents visible in the account's creative performance: aesthetic self-investment (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES, PEPTIDE all delivering CPA $1.50–$2.29) and career/income reinvention (DREAMCAREER, ESCAPE, FREETRAINING at CPA $1.64–$2.12). She does not fit a single-category profile — she is evaluating both personal transformation and economic empowerment simultaneously. Core identity: a woman in midlife who views both her appearance and her professional trajectory as domains where she still has agency and upside. Decision style is aspiration-led but requires social or clinical proof before commitment. Key objections: 'Is this the right time for me?', 'Is the quality/provider trustworthy?', 'Can I actually make this change at my stage?'. She is loss-averse about wasted time and money, and responds to framing that validates her as the protagonist of a transformation rather than as someone who needs to be fixed.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Female, age 45–54, is the single highest-volume purchase-converting demographic in the account: 1,270 results at CPA $5.67 (Website purchases result type) from reach 167,732 and impressions 183,549, with CTR 2.03% and CVR 34.2% — sourced from the demographic report at 95.7% spend coverage. Facebook Feed is the primary volume and efficiency placement at $4.39 CPA across 1,503 results (vs. Instagram Feed at $5.08 CPA across 1,082 results). This segment is mobile-primary given Advantage+ placement mix. Geography is inferred as US-based from city-token ad clusters (NYC, CHI, ATL, CLE, DEN, DAL). Female 35–44 is the second-largest purchase segment (1,056 results, CPA $5.30) and shares structural characteristics; this profile intentionally focuses on the 45–54 peak-performance band to avoid conflating two potentially distinct cohorts.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Test this ICP as the anchor for a cross-pillar creative that combines career-transformation aspiration with aesthetic confidence framing in a single ad — e.g., 'Look and earn your best at 45+'. This has not been tested in the account and represents a low-cost creative hypothesis that could capture dual-intent at TOFU. Assign to a counter-diagonal cell (e.g., C1D) in the Matrix Sprint Test to isolate the combined-angle concept against single-angle controls in the same row. Keep CTA 'free access' framing for lead capture. Use Facebook Feed as primary; do not manually restrict to single placement.
