conversion_tracking_signal.note: Conversion-based tracking: funnel actions are attributed to the converting device/platform/placement. Spend and impressions are not device-attributable under this tracking, so no CPA/CTR exist here. The export window may differ from the account's campaign window — treat cross-surface comparisons as directional.

message_pillars.label: Feed-First Engagement Anchor
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Establish a baseline creative that captures attention in the Feed placement — the only placement with confirmed engagement volume (33 link clicks, 6 adds-to-cart) — using a hook-forward format that stops the scroll before asking for any downstream action.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Feed placement drove 33 link clicks and 6 adds-to-cart vs. Threads feed's 3 link clicks and 1 add-to-cart. No cost-per-result or CVR data is available at this stage; these are raw funnel counts only. C3 absorbed the largest spend share (≈$27.44 of ≈$57.97 total) but results are not yet attributed to concepts, so concept-level CPA cannot be stated.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU: thumbstop and link-click generation in Feed. The creative must earn the click before any downstream metric is meaningful. Add-to-cart volume (6 events) is too small for conversion optimization; link-click volume is the actionable early signal.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Lead with a problem-statement hook in the first 2–3 seconds (HK_Problem). Body copy follows PAS structure — agitate the pain before presenting relief. Tone stays relatable and peer-level, not aspirational or clinical. Avoid price or offer language until terminal metric is confirmed.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements with Feed as the expected delivery anchor given observed traffic concentration. Broad targeting, ABO budget. Do not restrict to Feed manually — let Advantage+ allocate, but monitor Feed vs. Threads split in reporting.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Wait for at minimum 50 link clicks per concept before drawing CPA conclusions. Scale spend only after results (terminal metric) begin populating — current data volume is pre-statistical.

message_pillars.label: Concept Spend Efficiency Audit
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: C3 received disproportionate spend (≈$27.44, ~47% of total) relative to C1 (≈$12.90), C4 (≈$13.66), and C2 (≈$3.97), yet no results are attributed to any concept. The next sprint must structurally equalize spend across columns to produce readable concept-level cost-per-result signals before any scaling decision is made.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: C3 spend ≈$27.44; C4 ≈$13.66; C1 ≈$12.90; C2 ≈$3.97. Results, CPA, and CVR are null for all four concepts in the rollup. C2's severely suppressed spend ($3.97) means it is statistically unreadable. No variable-level performance data exists to ground concept-quality judgments.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU: the matrix sprint is itself the test vehicle. Each concept column must generate enough link clicks and eventual results to be comparable. MOFU angles (feature-benefit, comparison) are appropriate for audiences who have already registered a problem and are evaluating options.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: In the MST grid, assign one concept angle per column and enforce equal ABO budgets per ad set so no single concept drifts to C3-level dominance in early delivery. Design each column's creative to be meaningfully distinct — different format, different hook type — so spend differences, when they emerge, reflect genuine audience preference rather than auction-level similarity penalties.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: ABO with equal budgets per column ad set. Advantage+ placements active on all four. Monitor concept-level spend pacing in the first 48 hours and flag any column absorbing >40% of total spend as a potential delivery anomaly, not necessarily a performance signal.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Do not pause C2-equivalent low-spend columns in the first 7 days. Delivery suppression on a low-spend concept may reflect creative similarity scoring or auction overlap, not audience rejection. Allow the full sprint window before making structural cuts.

message_pillars.label: iPhone / Mobile-Native Social Proof
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: iPhone is the dominant device in the conversion funnel (13 + 33 link clicks across two iPhone rows vs. no other device data). A mobile-native creative format (vertical video or UGC-style) with embedded social proof should lower friction for this device cohort and improve the link-click-to-add-to-cart conversion rate beyond the observed ~15% (6 ATC / 39 total iPhone link clicks).
message_pillars.why_it_matters: iPhone accounts for all recorded link clicks (46 total across two device rows: 13 and 33) and all 7 recorded adds-to-cart (1 + 6). No other device appears in the conversion data. The blended iPhone ATC rate is approximately 15% (7/46) — directional only given low volume. No cost or CPA data is device-attributed.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU-to-MOFU bridge: UGC social proof is optimized to generate the first click (TOFU) while the embedded proof element seeds credibility for the downstream action (MOFU). On mobile, native-feeling content outperforms polished studio formats in thumbstop rate.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. First frame must feel native to a phone scroll — no broadcast-style opening. Social proof element (testimonial quote, review count, or peer endorsement) appears within the first 3 seconds. Copy kept short for mobile thumb-scroll pacing. Avoid heavy text overlays that obscure on small screens.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements; the vertical format will be favored by Reels and Stories alongside Feed. Do not artificially restrict to Feed despite Feed's current traffic dominance — mobile-native formats may unlock Reels inventory and broaden reach.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Track iPhone ATC rate as the early proxy. If this pillar's cells produce ATC rates materially above the baseline ~15%, flag for budget increase. Confirm terminal metric before scaling to avoid optimizing toward ATC when the real goal may differ.

message_pillars.label: Threads Feed Exploratory Expansion
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Threads feed delivered 3 link clicks and 1 add-to-cart from minimal activity, suggesting the placement is live and converting at a surface-level rate comparable to Facebook Feed (1/3 = 33% ATC rate vs. 6/33 = 18% on Facebook Feed) — though sample sizes are too small for statistical confidence. A dedicated exploratory concept column should test whether Threads-native copy and format conventions can produce a lower cost-per-result than Facebook Feed given potentially lower CPM competition.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Threads feed: 3 link clicks, 1 add-to-cart (~33% ATC rate, n=3, pre-statistical). Facebook Feed: 33 link clicks, 6 adds-to-cart (~18% ATC rate, n=33, still low volume). No spend, CPM, or CPA is broken out by placement in the available data. This pillar is explicitly exploratory and low-confidence.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU: Threads audiences skew toward discovery and conversational content. An unaware-level hook with curiosity framing matches the ambient browsing behavior typical of Threads feed. Avoid hard-sell CTAs until the placement's conversion behavior is better understood.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Text-weight, conversational format optimized for the Threads feed aesthetic (less visual-dominant than Facebook Feed). Hook framed as a question or observation rather than a direct claim. Keep creative concise — Threads users skim fast. This column is flagged as EXPLORATORY in the matrix; avatar_basis is exploratory with no historical ICP grounding.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements will naturally distribute to Threads. Do not force Threads-only delivery — instead, monitor Threads share of delivery in the placement breakdown and compare ATC rates once link-click volume exceeds 30 per placement.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Low priority for budget allocation until volume supports a verdict. Treat this column as a signal-gathering cell, not a scaling candidate, in the first sprint.

active_hypotheses.label: A problem-first hook (HK_Problem) in the opening frame will produce a higher link-click rate than a benefit-first hook (HK_Benefit) across all four concept columns, because the account's funnel data shows users entering at an add-to-cart stage consistent with problem-aware rather than solution-aware awareness levels.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 1 (Feed-First Engagement Anchor) — HK_Problem baseline
active_hypotheses.risk: Low sample volume may prevent statistical significance within a single sprint. The ~15% blended ATC rate suggests post-click quality matters as much as click volume — hook wins on CTR may not translate to cost-per-result wins.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Row A of the MST uses HK_Problem across C1A, C2A, C3A, C4A (four different avatars/concepts, same hook type). Row B uses HK_Benefit across C1B, C2B, C3B, C4B. All other variables (FW_, TN_, PR_) differ within each row so hook is the only shared variable.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_ hook type (HK_Problem vs. HK_Benefit). Distributed as: Row A = HK_Problem constant across all 4 columns; Row B = HK_Benefit constant across all 4 columns. Each hook type appears exactly 4 times in varied concept/tone/framework contexts, satisfying the 2–4 appearance rule and enabling cross-avatar hook isolation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: Row A (HK_Problem) achieves a link-click rate (link clicks / impressions) at least 20% higher than Row B (HK_Benefit) after each row accumulates ≥200 impressions. Secondary: ATC rate directionally favors HK_Problem.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. Problem-aware messaging is directionally supported by the funnel entry data (users reaching ATC), but without demographic or creative variable data, the magnitude of the hook effect is unknown.

active_hypotheses.label: Equalizing ABO budgets across all four concept columns (C1–C4) will reveal a readable cost-per-result signal per concept within one sprint, whereas the current unequal spend distribution (C3 at ~47% of total) has produced null results across all concept rows.
active_hypotheses.source: Current spend distribution: C3 ≈$27.44, C4 ≈$13.66, C1 ≈$12.90, C2 ≈$3.97 — all showing null results.
active_hypotheses.risk: Meta's delivery algorithm may still favor one concept via auction dynamics even with equal budgets. If one column receives far lower CPM, its link-click volume will differ despite equal spend — this is a signal, not a flaw.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Next sprint: set equal ABO daily budgets for all four concept column ad sets. Target minimum $10–15/day per column for ≥7 days to generate actionable link-click volume (target ≥50 link clicks per concept before reading CPA).
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: Budget allocation structure (equal ABO per column vs. uncontrolled delivery weighting). This is a structural/methodological variable, not a creative variable — it is held constant as equal across all 16 cells and is not an angle variable in the matrix rows. Its effect is read at the concept-column level by comparing spend distribution after 7 days.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: No single column absorbs more than 35% of total sprint spend after Day 3. All four columns reach ≥50 link clicks by Day 7. At least two columns produce a non-null cost-per-result.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High structural impact. Without readable concept-level data, no creative or audience scaling decision is defensible. This is the foundational fix that enables all other hypotheses to be tested.

active_hypotheses.label: A UGC-style, mobile-native creative format (CN_UGC) will produce a higher add-to-cart rate than a polished/designed format (CN_Lifestyle or CN_ProductDemo) on iPhone, because iPhone accounts for 100% of observed device-side conversion events and native-feeling content reduces perceived ad friction on mobile feeds.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 3 (iPhone / Mobile-Native Social Proof) — current blended iPhone ATC rate of ~15% (7 ATC / 46 link clicks, pre-statistical).
active_hypotheses.risk: The account may not be an e-commerce/purchase model — 'adds-to-cart' may be a proxy metric rather than the terminal result. If the real terminal metric differs, ATC rate optimization may be misleading. Flag for cohort configuration before acting on this hypothesis at scale.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Column C3 of the MST uses CN_UGC as the concept constant (Column Constant) across all four rows (C3A, C3B, C3C, C3D). Column C1 uses a polished/designed concept constant (CN_Lifestyle or CN_ProductDemo). All row-level angle variables (FW_, TN_, HK_) differ across rows within each column.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: CN_ format angle (CN_UGC vs. CN_Lifestyle/CN_ProductDemo) held constant within its respective column. Appears 4 times each (once per row within its column), across varied framework/tone/hook contexts in the rows — satisfying the 2–4 distribution rule at the column level. Effect readable by comparing ATC rates between the two columns on iPhone delivery.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: CN_UGC column produces an ATC rate ≥25% higher than the comparison column on iPhone (absolute: >19% ATC rate vs. baseline ~15%) after ≥30 link clicks per column on iPhone devices.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. Mobile-native UGC is a broadly validated format signal, but the account's low data volume means the effect size estimate is speculative.

active_hypotheses.label: A curiosity-based hook (HK_Curiosity) will outperform a social-proof hook (HK_SocialProof) in link-click rate for audiences at the Unaware or Problem-Aware stage (AW_Unaware, AW_ProblemAware), because curiosity gaps create intrinsic motivation to click without requiring prior category knowledge.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 4 (Threads Feed Exploratory) — HK_Curiosity baseline in the exploratory column.
active_hypotheses.risk: HK_SocialProof may underperform on CTR but produce higher downstream quality (ATC rate). A hook that generates curious clicks may attract lower-intent users. Read both click rate and ATC rate together before drawing conclusions.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Row C of the MST uses HK_Curiosity constant across C1C, C2C, C3C, C4C. Row D uses HK_SocialProof constant across C1D, C2D, C3D, C4D. AW_ level is set to AW_Unaware or AW_ProblemAware for both rows. All other variables (FW_, TN_, CN_ format) differ within each row.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_ hook type (HK_Curiosity vs. HK_SocialProof) distributed as Row C vs. Row D. Each hook type appears 4 times across 4 different avatar/concept columns, satisfying isolation requirements. The counter-diagonal (C1D, C2C, C3B, C4A) should be monitored for cross-variable interaction effects.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: Row C (HK_Curiosity) achieves link-click rate ≥15% higher than Row D (HK_SocialProof) after ≥200 impressions per row. If the Threads placement delivers on Row C cells, compare Threads-specific CTR as a secondary signal.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium-low. This is a directional hypothesis with no prior creative variable data to anchor the prediction. Treat as signal-gathering in Sprint 1.

active_hypotheses.label: The main diagonal (C1A, C2B, C3C, C4D) — each carrying a TN_Relatable tone constant across four different avatar columns — will demonstrate whether relatable tonality is a universal signal or avatar-specific, because the diagonal isolates one variable (tone) across maximum concept diversity.
active_hypotheses.source: No prior tone variable data exists in the account. This hypothesis establishes the first tone baseline.
active_hypotheses.risk: Diagonal isolation is the highest-confidence structure in the matrix but requires all 4 avatar columns to generate sufficient volume simultaneously. If one column is suppressed (as C2 was at $3.97 in the prior period), the diagonal signal breaks.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Assign TN_Relatable as the shared tone variable on the main diagonal: C1A, C2B, C3C, C4D. Each cell also carries its column's ICP constant and a unique combination of FW_, HK_, HP_, and PR_ variables. The counter-diagonal uses TN_Aspirational for contrast isolation.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: TN_ tonality (TN_Relatable on main diagonal, TN_Aspirational on counter-diagonal). TN_Relatable appears exactly 4 times (main diagonal cells) across 4 different avatar/concept contexts. TN_Aspirational appears exactly 4 times (counter-diagonal cells). No other row or column shares either tone constant, preserving isolation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: If TN_Relatable cells produce a consistently higher link-click rate (≥2 of 4 diagonal cells outperforming their column's other rows) across at least 3 of the 4 avatar columns, tonality is flagged as a scalable variable. If the pattern is column-specific (e.g., only C3C outperforms), tone is an avatar-dependent signal.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High if volume is sufficient. Tone is a durable creative variable — a confirmed TN_Relatable signal would apply to all future sprint planning across avatars.

active_hypotheses.label: Adding an explicit pain-point reference in copy (HP_ variable active) will improve add-to-cart rate versus generic benefit copy (HP_ absent), because the funnel data shows users are entering at a problem-aware stage and pain acknowledgment reduces cognitive distance to action.
active_hypotheses.source: No prior HP_ variable data. Baseline is the blended ~15% ATC rate (7/46 iPhone link clicks, pre-statistical).
active_hypotheses.risk: Low volume is the primary risk. 7 total ATC events across the entire account is insufficient to detect a 5pp ATC rate difference with statistical confidence. This hypothesis is a directional signal-gathering exercise, not a confirmatory test.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: In Row B of the MST, assign one explicit HP_ tag per cell (HP_Time, HP_Money, HP_Confidence, HP_Overwhelm — one per column, varied). In Row A (HK_Problem row), HP_ variables are absent to keep Row A clean for hook isolation. Compare Row B ATC rate to Row A ATC rate after controlling for hook type.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HP_ pain specificity (explicit pain label present vs. absent). HP_ tags appear in Row B only (4 cells, 4 different pain types across 4 columns). Each specific HP_ code appears exactly once — satisfying minimum distribution — with the understanding that pain-type comparison is secondary; the primary test is HP_present vs. HP_absent (Row B vs. Row A). Pain-type sub-analysis requires a future sprint with 2+ appearances per HP_ code.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: Row B (HP_ active) produces ATC rate ≥5 percentage points above Row A (HP_ absent) after ≥30 link clicks per row. Secondary: if one HP_ code (e.g., HP_Money) produces a materially higher ATC rate, flag it for 2× repetition in Sprint 2.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. Pain specificity is a well-established copy lever, but without knowing the terminal metric or the product category, the most resonant pain type is unknown.

icp_profiles.message_resonance: No creative variable data exists to confirm specific message resonance. Directionally, the Feed + iPhone combination suggests short-form, mobile-native formats (UGC, vertical video) and problem-acknowledgment hooks are the appropriate starting point. Social proof elements (PR_UGC, PR_Testimonial) are hypothesized to reduce friction given the mobile impulse context.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: All observed conversion events are iPhone-sourced, suggesting this group is both the most reachable and most conversion-active segment in the account. The blended ATC rate of ~15% (7/46) is directional but pre-statistical. No checkout or purchase data is available, so funnel depth beyond ATC is unknown. Urgency response and price sensitivity cannot be assessed from current evidence.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: Feed placement on Facebook (33 link clicks, 6 ATCs) is the primary observed entry point. Threads feed contributed a small share (3 link clicks, 1 ATC). Entry appears to occur at the problem-aware stage based on hook-to-action speed.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: This audience interacts with the account's ads in a mobile-first, ambient browsing context — they are not actively searching but can be interrupted by relevant content. Their conversion to add-to-cart suggests moderate to high intent upon click, though the terminal metric is unknown so purchase intent cannot be confirmed. They likely respond to content that feels native to their feed rather than overtly promotional. Pain recognition (problem-aware) appears to be the entry condition given the funnel entry pattern.

Gender, age, and geography are unknown — no demographic breakdown exists in the current evidence. Likely concentrated in Feed placements given Feed's 33/36 total link-click share. Device context suggests consumption in a mobile-native, thumb-scroll environment.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Assign this profile to the primary concept column (C1) in the MST with CN_UGC as the concept constant and HK_Problem as the Row A hook. However, the existence of conversion events from Threads confirms the placement is active and the pixel is firing. Urgency, price sensitivity, and funnel depth are completely unknown for this segment.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: Threads feed, likely at TOFU/unaware stage based on platform context. This audience has not been deliberately targeted — delivery was organic from Advantage+ auto-placement.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: Threads users tend to engage with opinion, commentary, and discovery content rather than direct-response advertising. This audience may be at an earlier awareness level (AW_Unaware or AW_ProblemAware) than the Facebook Feed cohort and requires softer entry-point messaging. They are likely resistant to aggressive CTAs but responsive to curiosity-gap and lifestyle-alignment content. No psychographic data is confirmed from this account.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Users reached via the Threads feed placement — 3 link clicks and 1 add-to-cart observed. No device, gender, age, or geography data is available for this segment specifically. Threads as a platform skews toward users already embedded in Meta's ecosystem who engage with text-forward, conversational content. Volume is extremely low and this profile is entirely exploratory.

message_pillars.label: High-Engagement Static Variant Scaling
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Static_V6 and C2_Static_V3 are the account's two strongest performers by CTR (1.61% and 0.85% respectively) and together account for $1,582.78 of $2,354.17 total spend. Before the result type is resolved, CTR and thumbstop are the only readable optimization signals. This pillar locks in the creative DNA of the top-performing static variants and systematically tests angle variables against that baseline to identify which creative dimensions drive click efficiency.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Static_V6: $603.68 spend, 10,909 impressions, 176 link clicks, CTR 1.61% — highest CTR in the account. C2_Static_V3: $979.10 spend, 37,204 impressions, 315 link clicks, CTR 0.85% — highest absolute click volume. Static_V1: $269.33 spend, 13,995 impressions, 100 clicks, CTR 0.71%. C2_Static_V2: $8.28 spend, 117 impressions, 5 clicks, CTR 4.27% — extreme CTR but only 117 impressions, statistically thin. No result-level data exists for any ad (result_type: unknown, results: 0 across all 11 ads), so cost per result cannot be computed. CTR is the sole early-funnel signal available.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU thumbstop and click-through efficiency. Until the terminal conversion event is mapped and firing, all optimization decisions should route through CTR and link-click volume as proxies for downstream intent.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Static format only (matching account's current library of 11 static ads). Treat Static_V6 creative treatment as the de-facto control. New variants should isolate one angle variable per cell (hook type, tone, or copy framework) while holding the static format constant. Avoid video or motion formats in this sprint until a baseline exists.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Run under Advantage+ auto-placements with ABO budgets per ad set. Audience Network Native/Banner/Interstitial generated the highest observed CTR (4.41%, $520.68 spend) and Instagram Feed the highest feed-native CTR (1.46%, $275.85 spend) — the system should be allowed to allocate toward these naturally. Do not pin placements manually; monitor placement breakdown post-launch for efficiency signals.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Once the terminal result event is mapped and accumulating data, re-rank all cells by cost per result rather than CTR. Until then, flag any cell achieving CTR >1.5% with >5,000 impressions as a provisional winner worthy of budget consolidation. Do not scale C2_Static_V2 despite its 4.27% CTR — 117 impressions is insufficient volume for a reliable signal.

message_pillars.label: Male 25–44 Primary Audience Dominance
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Demographic data shows males aged 25–34 and 35–44 are the dominant spend-receiving cohorts ($754.72 and $538.71 respectively out of $2,354.17 total, together representing ~54% of account spend). Their CTRs (0.78% and 0.88%) are mid-range but consistent. This pillar codifies the male 25–44 segment as the core ICP anchor for the matrix's C1 and C2 columns and directs creative angle variation specifically at this audience's likely psychographic drivers.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Male 25–34: $754.72 spend, 27,652 impressions, 216 link clicks, CTR 0.78%, reach 23,330. Male 35–44: $538.71 spend, 16,707 impressions, 147 link clicks, CTR 0.88%, reach 13,692. Combined these two cohorts received $1,293.43 spend (~55% of total). Male 45–54 shows the highest male CTR at 1.18% ($179.72 spend, 5,318 impressions, 63 clicks) — a secondary signal worth testing. Female cohorts are under-invested (female 25–34: $174.97; female 35–44: $139.40) but show comparable or higher CTRs (1.07% and 1.22% respectively), suggesting potential efficiency upside. All demographic data is at account-aggregate level with no result attribution — CTR comparisons only.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU through MOFU. The male 25–44 block should carry the matrix's highest-confidence concept columns (C1 and C2). Angle rows should vary hook type and tone to identify which messaging register (rational-informational vs. assertive-benefit-led) drives stronger click intent within this demographic.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting under Advantage+ with ABO. Facebook Reels (combined: $831.18 spend across FB Reels placements) and Instagram Feed ($275.85) are the primary delivery environments for this demographic profile. Allow the system to optimize placement allocation; monitor demographic × placement cross-tab post-launch if the platform exposes it.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Male 45–54 (CTR 1.18%) is a candidate for a dedicated exploratory column in a future sprint if male 25–44 columns establish a cost-per-result baseline. Do not break it into a separate column this sprint — evidence volume is too thin ($179.72 spend, 63 clicks) to justify independent column treatment.

message_pillars.label: Female Audience Efficiency Unlock
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Female cohorts are significantly under-invested relative to their CTR performance. Female 45–54 posts the highest CTR of any female segment at 1.94% on $67.79 spend. Female 25–34 (1.07%) and 35–44 (1.22%) both outperform their male counterparts on a CTR basis despite receiving only 23% of total spend collectively ($382.16 of $2,354.17). This pillar tests whether dedicated female-oriented creative — with appropriately adjusted messaging tone, pain points, and visual register — can unlock a lower cost per result than the male-dominant baseline, once the result event is resolved.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Female 45–54: CTR 1.94%, $67.79 spend, 1,389 impressions, 27 clicks, reach 1,205. Female 35–44: CTR 1.22%, $139.40 spend, 3,775 impressions, 46 clicks. Female 25–34: CTR 1.07%, $174.97 spend, 4,670 impressions, 50 clicks. All three female segments outperform their exact male age-band counterparts on CTR (male 45–54: 1.18%; male 35–44: 0.88%; male 25–34: 0.78%). Total female spend across all segments: ~$463.58 (~20% of total). No result-level data exists — CTR comparison only. Confidence is low for causal claims; this is a directional hypothesis requiring a dedicated test column.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU entry with MOFU-ready messaging. Female audiences may be SolutionAware rather than purely ProblemAware if the product/service category is familiar — test both AW_ProblemAware and AW_SolutionAware hooks across the row variables in this column.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Instagram Feed (CTR 1.46%) and Instagram Stories (CTR 1.28%) are the most click-efficient placements in the account and likely index toward female audiences. Under Advantage+ auto-placements, the system should naturally weight toward these; do not restrict placements but flag Instagram Feed performance in post-launch breakdowns.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: This column should launch at a modest ABO budget (exploratory allocation) and be judged first on CTR parity with the male columns, then on cost per result once the conversion event fires. If female CTR at scale (>10,000 impressions per cell) matches or exceeds male CTR, increase budget to parity and await result data.

message_pillars.label: Concept C2 Architecture Isolation
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: The account's only named concept grouping is 'C2' with $1,125.45 spend across its variants (C2_Static_V1 through V5), representing ~48% of total account spend. However, within C2, performance varies significantly: C2_Static_V3 (CTR 0.85%, $979.10) dominates volume while C2_Static_V2 (CTR 4.27%, $8.28) shows an extreme outlier CTR on minimal impressions. The C2 concept's internal variable structure is unknown from ad names alone. This pillar treats C2 as a concept constant to isolate and maps the remaining angle variables (hook, tone, framework) across rows to understand what within C2 drives click behavior.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: C2 concept total: $1,125.45 spend, concept_rollup confirms this. C2_Static_V3: $979.10 spend, 37,204 impressions, 315 clicks, CTR 0.85%. C2_Static_V4: $49.10 spend, 726 impressions, 9 clicks, CTR 1.24%. C2_Static_V5: $65.10 spend, 2,143 impressions, 12 clicks, CTR 0.56%. C2_Static_V1: $23.87 spend, 1,423 impressions, 7 clicks, CTR 0.49%. C2_Static_V2: $8.28 spend, 117 impressions, 5 clicks, CTR 4.27% — extreme outlier, insufficient impressions for reliability. Non-C2 static variants (V1–V6) total: $1,045.27 spend. No result data available for any variant.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU engagement and click qualification. C2_Static_V3's high click volume ($979.10, 315 clicks) suggests this concept format may be attracting higher-intent clickers — a MOFU-relevant hypothesis once result tracking is resolved.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Audience Network Native/Banner/Interstitial generated the account's highest placement CTR at 4.41% ($520.68 spend) and is likely capturing a portion of C2 delivery. Under Advantage+ broad targeting, continue allowing Audience Network allocation but monitor whether it contributes quality clicks once a downstream event fires.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: C2_Static_V3 has sufficient impression volume (37,204) to be treated as a stable creative baseline. Use it as the control reference for all C2-column hypotheses. Do not reallocate its budget until a challenger within the matrix exceeds its CTR at equivalent impression volume (>30,000 impressions).

active_hypotheses.label: Replacing a benefit-led hook (HK_Benefit) with a problem-first hook (HK_Problem) on static ads served to the male 25–44 cohort will increase link CTR by at least 20% relative to the Static_V6 baseline, because the account's male-dominant audience may be ProblemAware rather than SolutionAware and will engage more readily with pain-point framing.
active_hypotheses.source: Static_V6 (CTR 1.61%, 10,909 impressions, $603.68 spend — highest CTR static in the account)
active_hypotheses.risk: Low confidence that CTR alone predicts cost per result. A problem-first hook may attract curiosity clicks from users who do not convert, inflating CTR without downstream value. This risk cannot be mitigated until the result event fires.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: New static creative matched to Static_V6's visual register and copy length, with the opening headline rewritten as a direct pain-point statement (HK_Problem) rather than a benefit claim. All other elements held constant.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_Hook type: HK_Problem vs. HK_Benefit. In the MST matrix this variable appears in cells C1A (HK_Problem) and C1B (HK_Benefit control) within the male 25–44 column (C1), and is repeated in C2A (HK_Problem) and C2B (HK_Benefit) within the C2 concept column — giving the variable 4 appearances across 2 different concept contexts, satisfying the 2–4 distribution rule. Rows A and B each share their respective hook type while all other angle variables (FW_, TN_, AW_) differ across columns.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: HK_Problem cell achieves link CTR ≥1.93% (≥20% above Static_V6's 1.61%) at a minimum of 8,000 impressions per cell within the sprint window. Secondary: if result tracking is resolved mid-sprint, the HK_Problem cell must also show cost per result ≤ HK_Benefit control.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. Hook framing is a high-leverage variable in early-funnel static ads. If the male 25–44 audience is primarily ProblemAware (consistent with their mid-range CTR on existing benefit-led creatives), a problem-first hook could meaningfully improve thumbstop and click rates.

active_hypotheses.label: A warm, lifestyle-oriented tone (TN_Warm + CN_Lifestyle) directed at female audiences will produce higher link CTR than the account's existing assertive/direct static variants when served to female 25–44 users, because female cohorts currently show higher CTR than male counterparts despite receiving male-oriented creative — suggesting messaging-audience misalignment.
active_hypotheses.source: Account-wide female 25–44 blended CTR of ~1.13% (female 25–34: 1.07%, female 35–44: 1.22%) on $314.37 combined spend — no female-specific creative exists as a named control; this is a baseline-from-demographics comparison.
active_hypotheses.risk: Medium. Without result data, a CTR improvement in the female column cannot be confirmed as cost-per-result improvement. Additionally, broad targeting under Advantage+ may still predominantly serve male audiences, making female-audience attribution from demographic breakdowns necessary but not guaranteed at cell level.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: New static creative in the C3 column (female-oriented exploratory ICP) using CN_Lifestyle visual framing, TN_Warm copy tone, FW_BAB framework, and HK_Benefit hook. The creative should visually and linguistically signal relevance to a female audience without demographic micro-targeting — rely on Advantage+ broad delivery to route toward the female segment.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: TN_Tonality: TN_Warm (female column C3) vs. TN_Assertive (male column C1) and TN_Rational (male column C2). TN_Warm appears in cells C3A, C3B, C3C, C3D (constant across the C3 column as a concept constant) and is contrasted against TN_Assertive in C1 and TN_Rational in C2, giving a cross-column tonality read across 3 different ICP contexts. Row D of the counter diagonal (C1D, C2C, C3B, C4A) carries TN_Warm as the diagonal variable for cross-avatar isolation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C3 column cells achieve average link CTR ≥1.40% at ≥5,000 impressions each, exceeding the current female blended CTR of 1.13%. If demographic breakdowns are available post-launch, ≥40% of C3 column impressions should be served to female audiences by Advantage+ without manual targeting.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium-high. Female cohorts show a consistent CTR premium over male cohorts in this account. Purpose-built female creative could amplify this efficiency signal and open a new audience pool at competitive cost per result.

active_hypotheses.label: Adding a social proof element (PR_SocialProof or PR_Testimonial) to static ads in the C2 concept column will increase link CTR relative to C2_Static_V3's baseline of 0.85%, because the C2 concept currently has no named proof variable and may be underperforming due to a credibility gap at the awareness stage.
active_hypotheses.source: C2_Static_V3 (CTR 0.85%, 37,204 impressions, 315 clicks, $979.10 spend — highest volume C2 variant and the account's highest-click ad)
active_hypotheses.risk: Low-medium. The C2 concept's baseline CTR (0.85%) may be suppressed by placement mix (C2_Static_V3 received 37,204 impressions, heavily weighted toward Reels where CTRs are structurally lower). The social proof test result may reflect placement efficiency rather than proof element efficacy. Monitor placement breakdown for C2C.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: New C2-concept static variant (C2 column, row C) incorporating a PR_SocialProof overlay — e.g. a user count, rating badge, or quoted outcome statement — added to the existing C2_Static_V3 visual structure. All other copy, CTA, and design elements held constant relative to C2_Static_V3.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: PR_Proof type: PR_SocialProof (new variant, C2C) vs. no proof element (C2_Static_V3 baseline, C2A control). PR_SocialProof also appears in C3C and C4C (row C shared variable), so the proof variable is distributed across 3 cells in row C spanning 3 different concept columns — readable as a row-level signal. The variable appears 0 times in rows A, B, D to prevent over-representation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C2C (PR_SocialProof variant) achieves link CTR ≥1.05% (≥24% above C2_Static_V3's 0.85%) at ≥15,000 impressions. This threshold is set at a level that would make the proof variant competitive with Static_V6's 1.61% CTR on a comparable impression base.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. Social proof is a high-frequency performance driver in static ad creative. Given the C2 concept's scale ($1,125.45 spend) even a modest CTR lift on this concept column would have meaningful click-volume impact.

active_hypotheses.label: A curiosity-led hook (HK_Curiosity) will outperform a shock-based hook (HK_Shock) on thumbstop and link CTR across the main diagonal of the matrix (C1A, C2B, C3C, C4D), isolating the hook variable across all four avatar columns simultaneously for the highest-confidence read on hook type.
active_hypotheses.source: No direct hook-type control exists in the current ad library — ad names (Static_V1 through V6, C2_Static_V1 through V5) do not expose hook taxonomy. This hypothesis establishes the first isolated hook comparison in the account.
active_hypotheses.risk: Medium. Curiosity hooks can generate exploratory clicks from low-intent users, artificially inflating CTR without improving downstream results. Until the result event is resolved this comparison remains CTR-only. HK_Shock hooks risk platform policy friction on certain placements — copy must be reviewed against Meta ad policies before launch.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Main diagonal cells (C1A, C2B, C3C, C4D) each carry HK_Curiosity as the single shared row variable, implemented as an open-loop headline that withholds the payoff. Counter-diagonal cells (C4A, C3B, C2C, C1D) carry HK_Shock as the alternative hook. All other variables (FW_, TN_, AW_, CN_ format) differ across the diagonal cells — the hook type is the only constant.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_Hook type: HK_Curiosity appears exactly 4 times (C1A, C2B, C3C, C4D — main diagonal). HK_Shock appears exactly 4 times (C4A, C3B, C2C, C1D — counter diagonal). Each hook type is tested across all 4 avatar columns in fully varied creative contexts, producing the matrix's highest-confidence variable isolation. No other row or column shares both hook types — clean isolation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: HK_Curiosity cells achieve a mean link CTR ≥15% higher than HK_Shock cells at a combined minimum of 20,000 impressions per hook group (5,000+ per cell). Secondary: HK_Curiosity cells should show lower CPM-adjusted cost per click, indicating the hook drives genuine intent rather than accidental clicks.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High. Hook type is the single most upstream creative lever and the diagonal placement gives this variable the most statistically powerful read in the entire matrix. A clear signal here will inform hook selection for all future sprints regardless of avatar or concept.

active_hypotheses.label: An aspirational tone (TN_Aspirational) paired with a solution-aware message (AW_SolutionAware) will produce lower cost per result than a problem-first entry (TN_Assertive + AW_ProblemAware) for the male 25–44 audience once the conversion event is mapped, because the 35–44 male cohort's slightly higher CTR (0.88%) vs. 25–34 (0.78%) may signal a more SolutionAware, outcome-focused mindset.
active_hypotheses.source: Male 35–44 demographic aggregate: CTR 0.88%, $538.71 spend, 16,707 impressions, 147 clicks. This is a demographic-level baseline, not a cell-level control — confidence is low.
active_hypotheses.risk: Medium-high. This hypothesis tests two variables simultaneously (tonality + awareness stage), which reduces isolation purity. Treat findings as directional rather than conclusive. Additionally, the demographic CTR difference (0.88% vs. 0.78%) is small and may not be statistically meaningful at current impression volumes.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: C1C cell: male 25–44 column (C1), row C shared variable TN_Aspirational + AW_SolutionAware. Creative leads with an outcome or transformation image/headline rather than a pain statement. C1D cell uses TN_Assertive + AW_ProblemAware as the within-column contrast. All other variables (FW_, HK_, PR_) differ between C1C and C1D.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: TN_Tonality × AW_Awareness combination: TN_Aspirational + AW_SolutionAware (C1C, C2D) vs. TN_Assertive + AW_ProblemAware (C1D, C2C). Each combination appears exactly twice in different concept column contexts, satisfying the 2–4 distribution rule. Row C shares TN_Aspirational + AW_SolutionAware across C1C, C2C, and C3C — NOTE: only one of these two variables should be the true isolated variable per row; the primary isolation is TN_Aspirational (tonality), with AW_SolutionAware treated as a co-varying secondary. This should be noted as a two-variable combination test rather than a pure single-variable isolation — a known constraint given the account's early-stage evidence base.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: Once the result event fires and accumulates ≥20 results per cell, TN_Aspirational + AW_SolutionAware cell(s) must show cost per result ≤80% of TN_Assertive + AW_ProblemAware cell(s) at equivalent spend. Pre-result proxy: TN_Aspirational cells achieve CTR ≥0.95% (above male 25–44 current 0.88%) at ≥8,000 impressions.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. Awareness-stage alignment is a high-leverage creative dimension for mid-funnel efficiency. If the male 35–44 sub-cohort is genuinely more SolutionAware, aspirational messaging could meaningfully reduce cost per result versus pain-first alternatives.

active_hypotheses.label: Dedicating the matrix's fourth concept column (C4) to an exploratory older-male audience (45–54) with a rational, data-driven creative angle will generate a measurable CTR signal to determine whether this cohort warrants a dedicated concept column in a future sprint, given its account-best male CTR of 1.18% on modest spend.
active_hypotheses.source: Male 45–54 demographic aggregate: CTR 1.18%, $179.72 spend, 5,318 impressions, 63 clicks — thin evidence base, below the volume threshold for reliable conclusions.
active_hypotheses.risk: Low-medium. This is an explicitly exploratory column with no expectation of immediate efficiency. The main risk is budget dilution — ABO allocation for C4 should be set lower than C1 and C2 columns until the CTR signal is established. Advantage+ broad delivery may under-serve the 45–54 segment if the algorithm routes toward the account's established 25–34 delivery pattern.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: C4 column: exploratory avatar (Male 45–54, avatar_basis: exploratory, no historical cell data). Column constants: CN_ICP_MaleProfessional45-54, CN_Design_Clean, CTA family aligned to the product's core action. Row variables across C4A–C4D: vary FW_ (FW_FAB, FW_StoryBrand, FW_Direct, FW_PAS) while holding TN_Rational constant as the C4 column tone constant. PR_DataDriven and PR_Expert proof elements should appear in at least 2 of the 4 C4 cells.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: Avatar/ICP: Male 45–54 exploratory segment (C4 column, all rows). This is a column-constant isolation — all 4 C4 cells share the same avatar while varying framework across rows. The avatar variable is compared at the column level against C1 (male 25–44), C2 (C2 concept), and C3 (female exploratory). The C4 column is explicitly flagged as exploratory with no historical performance data; findings are hypothesis-generating for Sprint 2, not conclusive in Sprint 1.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C4 column cells collectively achieve mean link CTR ≥1.00% at ≥15,000 combined impressions. If any single C4 cell exceeds CTR 1.50% at ≥5,000 impressions, the male 45–54 avatar is promoted to a core ICP column in the next sprint. If all C4 cells fall below 0.70% CTR, the avatar is deprioritized.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Low in Sprint 1 (exploratory by design), high in Sprint 2 if the hypothesis is confirmed. Male 45–54 is currently the account's highest-CTR male demographic segment, making it a credible candidate for a dedicated column despite thin evidence.

icp_profiles.message_resonance: Current static ads (Static_V1 through V6, C2_Static_V1 through V5) are all performing in the 0.49%–1.61% CTR range for this cohort. Static_V6 (CTR 1.61%) represents the upper-bound creative performance. No concept-level or angle-level variable taxonomy has been applied to existing ads, so specific hook, tone, or framework preferences cannot be isolated. Rational (TN_Rational) and assertive (TN_Assertive) tones are reasonable starting hypotheses for the 35–44 sub-cohort; benefit-curiosity (HK_Curiosity + HK_Benefit) for the 25–34 sub-cohort.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: Both sub-cohorts are receiving the majority of static ad impressions and generating the bulk of link clicks (216 and 147 respectively out of 705 total). No funnel progression data exists beyond the click — conversion tracking shows zero attributed results, so post-click behavior is unknown. Price sensitivity and urgency response cannot be assessed without downstream data. The algorithm's consistent routing of budget to this segment across all 11 ads suggests stable engagement signals (thumbstop, hover, click) rather than a single creative spike.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU via paid static ads on Facebook and Instagram Reels/Feed. No MOFU or BOFU touchpoints are observable in the current data.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: This cohort is the account's revealed primary audience based on budget allocation patterns under broad targeting — the algorithm is selecting them without demographic restrictions, indicating they are engaging with the content at a rate sufficient to drive continued delivery. Their mid-range CTRs (0.78% for 25–34, 0.88% for 35–44) suggest they are engaging but not urgently so, which may point to ProblemAware or SolutionAware positioning rather than MostAware. The 35–44 sub-cohort's marginally higher CTR may reflect greater professional urgency, higher decision-making authority, or greater familiarity with the product category. Pain points are unknown without result or behavioral data; HP_Confidence and HP_Overwhelm are reasonable hypotheses for a professional male audience. Decision style likely skews rational-informational for the 35–44 group and benefit-curiosity for the 25–34 group.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Male, ages 25–44, combining the account's two highest-spend demographic segments. Male 25–34 received $754.72 spend (27,652 impressions, 23,330 reach) and male 35–44 received $538.71 spend (16,707 impressions, 13,692 reach) — together ~55% of total account spend. Primary delivery platforms are Facebook Reels (combined ~$831 spend) and Instagram Feed ($275.85). Device and geography data are not available in the current evidence set. Broad targeting under Advantage+ is routing the majority of budget to this cohort organically, suggesting strong algorithmic signal alignment.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Assign this ICP as the column constant for C1 (male 25–34 primary) and optionally C2 (male 35–44 with C2 concept architecture). In the MST matrix, vary hook type across rows A/B (HK_Problem vs. HK_Benefit) and tone across rows C/D (TN_Rational vs. TN_Assertive) to generate the first variable-level read on this cohort's creative preferences.

icp_profiles.message_resonance: No female-specific creative exists in the account. Based on CTR evidence, this segment responds to the current static format at above-average rates. Purpose-built creative using CN_Lifestyle visual framing, TN_Warm tone, FW_BAB framework, and PR_Testimonial or PR_SocialProof proof elements is the untested hypothesis. campaign_summary.data_caveat: Totals cover the full imported window 2026-03-01 → 2026-07-13.

conversion_tracking_signal.note: Conversion-based tracking: funnel actions are attributed to the converting device/platform/placement. Spend and impressions are not device-attributable under this tracking, so no CPA/CTR exist here. The export window may differ from the account's campaign window — treat cross-surface comparisons as directional.

message_pillars.label: Feed-First Conversion Driver
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Capitalise on Feed placements' dominant share of adds-to-cart and checkout initiations across all device types. Feed rows account for the overwhelming majority of funnel depth signals in the data (e.g., Feed placement rows show 26, 19, 21, 15, 12, 8 adds-to-cart vs. single digits for Stories/Reels). Anchor the matrix's highest-confidence concept columns in Feed-optimised creative formats that maximise thumbstop and carry the user through intent milestones.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Feed placements drove the bulk of conversion-adjacent activity: top Feed rows recorded 26, 21, 19, 15, 12 adds-to-cart and checkout initiations of 6, 7, 5, 5 respectively. The sole confirmed purchase in the placement data also occurred on a Feed row (7 link_clicks, 8 adds_to_cart, 1 purchase). Instagram Stories, Reels, and Facebook Reels each show 1–5 adds-to-cart per row and ≤2 checkout initiations. No purchase is attributed to non-Feed placements. C3 has the lowest CPA (€11.04) and highest CVR (21.6%), suggesting its creative/format approach is best converting within Feed.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU–BOFU: creatives assume problem-awareness and move user from consideration to checkout. Feed format allows copy depth, multi-image carousels, or video with clear CTA.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Optimise aspect ratios for Feed (1:1 or 4:5). Lead with a benefit hook in the first 3 seconds/frames. Include explicit price or value anchor. CTA family: 'Shop Now' / 'See Why X People Chose skov'. Advantage+ placements ON — let the algorithm weight Feed where signals are strongest, but do not exclude other placements to preserve learning.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Run under Advantage+ auto-placements (broad, ABO). Feed will self-select as primary delivery based on historical conversion signals. Do not manually pin to Feed-only — allow Stories/Reels to receive impressions and observe if CVR pattern persists.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Once a Feed-optimised cell wins on CTR/thumbstop signal within 3–5 days and ≥500 impressions, flag for budget reallocation to that ABO ad set. C3's CPA (€11.04) is the current benchmark floor; target ≤€11 CPA at scale before duplicating.

message_pillars.label: C3 Concept Expansion — Low-CPA Angle Scaling
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: C3 is the highest-efficiency concept in the account (CPA €11.04, CVR 21.6% link-click-to-result) despite the lowest spend (€88.29) and only 8 results. The priority is to stress-test whether C3's angle holds at higher spend and across varied tone/hook combinations, before declaring it a scaling winner. This pillar dedicates one matrix column to C3-derivative creatives and systematically rotates the angle variables to isolate what is driving efficiency.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: C3: spend €88.29, 8 results, CPA €11.04, CVR 21.6%. C1: spend €140.61, 9 results, CPA €15.62, CVR 2.8%. C2: spend €414.48, 17 results, CPA €24.38, CVR 6.5%. C3 is 55% cheaper per result than C1 and 55% cheaper than C2, on less than a quarter of C2's spend. Confidence in C3 is currently low due to small volume (8 results); this pillar is designed to build that confidence or falsify it.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU–MOFU: replicate the C3 angle at broader reach to test if CVR holds when impressions scale. Use value-stack and before/after framing to attract cold traffic that mirrors whoever responded to C3.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Keep the C3 concept constant (same design system, same CTA family) across all four cells in its matrix column. Vary FW_ and TN_ across rows A–D. Monitor whether ATC rate stays above the account average as spend crosses €150.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Do not restrict audience — the goal is to see if the C3 concept self-selects a winning audience segment organically.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: If C3-column cells sustain CPA ≤€13 after 15+ results, escalate budget 20% every 48 hours. If CPA drifts above €18 (C1 benchmark), pause and revert. Low confidence warning: 8 results is insufficient for statistical certainty; treat early scaling as a hypothesis, not a confirmed winner.

message_pillars.label: iPhone Checkout-Gap Bridge
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: iPhone is the dominant link-click device but shows a disproportionate gap between adds-to-cart and purchases. Across iPhone rows, adds-to-cart total 72 and checkouts initiated total 20 against only 1 purchase. This signals a checkout abandonment or friction problem specific to the mobile-Safari / iPhone experience. A dedicated creative pillar targets this gap with BOFU messaging that reduces hesitation and drives the final conversion step.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: iPhone rows: 11+27+18+7+19+10+30+12 = 134 link_clicks; adds_to_cart: 5+8+16+4+3+12+17+7 = 72; checkouts_initiated: 2+2+4+1+2+2+5+2 = 20; purchases: 1 (only from the row with 10 link_clicks, 12 ATC, 2 checkouts). ATC-to-checkout rate on iPhone ≈ 28% (20/72). The single purchase row has ATC:link_click ratio of 1.2 — unusually high, suggesting that when intent is very strong on iPhone, conversion does close. iPad and Android also show similar checkout drop-off patterns but at lower volume.
message_pillars.funnel_application: BOFU: assume the viewer has already considered the product. Address final objections (risk, trust, delivery, returns). Urgency and social proof are the primary levers at this stage.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Creative should surface trust signals prominently: reviews, guarantees, easy returns, delivery promise. Copy framework: PAS — Problem (still haven't ordered?), Agitate (every day without it is X), Solution (here's why 500+ customers clicked buy). CTA: 'Complete Your Order' or 'Get Yours Today'. Keep creative concise — 15s video or single static with bold social-proof overlay. Note: this pillar assumes checkout friction is partly a creative/messaging problem; a parallel UX audit of the mobile checkout flow is recommended.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements, broad ABO. The algorithm will find recent site visitors and ATC non-converters if the pixel has sufficient data. Do not create manual retargeting audiences — rely on Advantage+ audience expansion to surface high-intent users.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Primary success signal is checkout-to-purchase rate, not CTR. Requires purchase volume to evaluate — do not call a winner until ≥5 purchases per cell variant. Low confidence warning: only 1 purchase is attributed in the entire dataset; purchase-level CPA analysis is not yet viable.

message_pillars.label: Exploratory Avatar Expansion — Instagram-Native Engagement
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Instagram platform rows show consistently competitive ATC rates relative to link clicks (e.g., 8 link_clicks → 5 ATC; 10 link_clicks → 4 ATC; 10 link_clicks → 15 ATC; 1 confirmed purchase on Instagram). However, no established ICP profile is available. This exploratory pillar tests a psychographic/behavioural avatar hypothesis — a visually-driven, mobile-first discovery shopper — using Instagram-native formats (Reels, Stories) to see if a distinct high-intent segment emerges separate from the Facebook Feed audience.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Instagram platform rows: purchases = 1 (8 link_clicks, 8 ATC, 1 purchase — 12.5% link-to-purchase rate, the highest in the dataset). Instagram rows also show ATC:link_click ratios of 0.63, 0.40, 1.50 (the 10/15 row), suggesting some Instagram contexts convert to ATC at rates exceeding Facebook. Facebook has higher absolute volume but Instagram shows at least one outlier efficiency point. All claims are low-confidence due to small sample size and absence of spend/impression data at the platform level.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU: cold discovery. Instagram-native UGC or creator-style video to stop the scroll for an audience with no prior brand exposure. The StoryBrand framework creates character identification quickly.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: 9:16 vertical video, 15–30 seconds, UGC aesthetic (no high-production polish). Hook in first 2 seconds must address a recognisable lifestyle moment. No hard sell — end with a soft CTA ('See how it works' / 'Find yours'). Mark this column clearly as EXPLORATORY in the matrix; avatar_basis is hypothesis only, no historical ICP data to validate.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements. The algorithm will route vertical video to Reels and Stories. Broad targeting — do not add interest or demographic constraints. Watch thumbstop rate and 3-second view rate as primary early signals before any purchase signal is available.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: This is an exploratory column. Do not scale based on ATC alone. Require ≥3 purchases or a CTR significantly above account average before increasing budget. Treat results as directional input for the next MST cycle's ICP definition.

active_hypotheses.label: Replacing a rational benefit-led hook (HK_Benefit) with a social-proof hook (HK_SocialProof) in Feed-optimised creatives will increase adds-to-cart rate, because the dataset's highest ATC:click rows correlate with contexts where trust/validation signals are prominent.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 1 — Feed-First Conversion Driver (CN_ProductDemo + HK_Benefit baseline)
active_hypotheses.risk: Social-proof hooks require credible, specific proof assets (real reviews, real numbers). If proof copy is generic, the hook loses its advantage. Also, small purchase volume means CPA comparison will not be statistically valid within a single sprint.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Swap HK_Benefit for HK_SocialProof across row B of the matrix (cells C1B, C2B, C3B, C4B), keeping all column constants (ICP/design/CTA) and FW_ fixed within each column. Row A retains HK_Benefit as the control row.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_ (Hook type): HK_Benefit (row A, 4 cells) vs HK_SocialProof (row B, 4 cells). Each hook type appears exactly 4 times across 4 different concept columns — meeting the 2–4 distribution rule and spanning all avatars for maximum-confidence isolation. No other row variable changes between rows A and B.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: HK_SocialProof row (B) achieves an ATC rate (adds_to_cart / link_clicks) at least 20% higher than HK_Benefit row (A) after each cell accumulates ≥50 link clicks. Secondary: checkout initiation rate ≥15% higher in row B.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium-high. The dataset shows ATC:click ratios vary widely (0.1 to 1.5+), suggesting hook quality is a significant lever. Social proof is a well-established conversion catalyst at MOFU stage.

active_hypotheses.label: Using a Before-After-Bridge (FW_BAB) copy framework instead of Features-Advantages-Benefits (FW_FAB) in the C3 concept column will sustain or improve CPA below €13 at higher spend, revealing whether C3's efficiency is framework-driven or concept-driven.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 2 — C3 Concept Expansion row A (FW_FAB baseline, CPA reference €11.04 from historical C3 data)
active_hypotheses.risk: Low result volume on C3 historically (8 total results) means the sprint may not generate enough purchase signals for CPA comparison. ATC rate will serve as the proxy metric. Risk of false positive if the C3 concept itself (not the framework) is the primary efficiency driver.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Row A of the C3 column uses FW_FAB (control). Row C of the C3 column uses FW_BAB. All other column constants remain identical (same design system, same CTA, same concept angle). Rows B and D of the C3 column use FW_PAS and FW_Direct respectively — giving 4 distinct framework tests within one column.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: FW_ (Copy framework): FW_FAB appears in C3A; FW_BAB appears in C3C. To satisfy distribution rules, FW_BAB also appears in one cell of another column (e.g., C1C) under a different ICP — so FW_BAB appears in 2 cells total across the matrix in different contexts, making it readable. FW_FAB similarly appears in 2 cells minimum.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: FW_BAB cell (C3C) achieves CPA ≤€13 after ≥5 results, and ATC rate within 10% of the C3A FW_FAB cell. If FW_BAB underperforms by >30% on ATC rate, flag FW_FAB as the framework driver of C3's historical efficiency.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. If FW_BAB matches or beats FW_FAB, it unlocks a replicable narrative structure across other concept columns. If it underperforms, it isolates the framework as a variable and directs future testing toward FAB refinement.

active_hypotheses.label: Applying TN_Urgent tonality in BOFU creatives targeting the iPhone checkout gap will increase checkout-to-implied-purchase rate compared to TN_Rational tonality, by reducing deliberation time at the final decision stage.

Additionally, the dataset has only 1 confirmed purchase — CPA-level validation will require extended run time beyond one sprint.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Row C across all 4 columns uses TN_Rational (control). Row D across all 4 columns uses TN_Urgent. message_pillars.label: Sigil & Brand Icon Motion — High-CTR Visual Identity
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Leverage the account's strongest performing visual assets — the PINKSIGILREEL and REDSIGILCLOSEUP tokens — which demonstrate both the lowest cost per result and the highest CTR among well-sampled creative clusters. This pillar establishes the brand's distinctive sigil/icon as the primary visual hook across all four concept columns, isolating whether the sigil format drives results independent of copy angle or ICP.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: PINKSIGILREEL: 22 results, CPA $9.78, CTR 2.997%, 24 unique ads, $215.15 spend. REDSIGILCLOSEUP: 38 results, CPA $20.69, CTR 2.021%, 39 unique ads, $786.32 spend. Both outperform the account's heavier-spend tokens like SKULLSADONFLOOR (53 results but CPA $23.38, CTR 1.347%, $1,239.06 spend) and UKIYOSTILLSHOWCASE (26 results, CPA $31.86, CTR 1.361%). CUT1 shows the highest CTR in the dataset at 4.615% with CPA $13.45 (6 results, 1 unique ad — low confidence but directionally strong). JUNKYARD at 12.5% CTR/$2.83 CPA is spend-minimal and unreliable.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU entry: the sigil/icon close-up acts as a thumbstop mechanism on Instagram Feed and Reels. The brand mark is unfamiliar to cold audiences, so the hook must be visual-first and curiosity-led before any copy framework can operate. This pillar should feed MOFU retargeting once volume is established.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Lead with a tight close-up or animated loop of the sigil/brand icon in the first 1–2 seconds. No product-first framing — let the icon carry the hook. Test static (REDSIGILCLOSEUP style) vs. motion reel (PINKSIGILREEL style) as the row-level variable. Copy should be minimal and assertive, not explanatory. Avoid catalog-style layouts (CATALOG token: 1 result, CPA $97.87, CTR 0.37%).
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Instagram Feed and Reels are the highest-converting placements per conversion_tracking data (Instagram dominates purchase and checkout_initiated rows vs. Facebook). Stories drove 1 purchase with 9 link clicks — keep in rotation but do not over-index.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: PINKSIGILREEL at $9.78 CPA across 24 ads is the strongest volume-adjusted signal in the account. Prioritise increasing spend concentration behind this token cluster before expanding to new angles. Once this pillar accumulates 50+ results per cell, cost per result becomes a reliable verdict signal.

message_pillars.label: Cinematic/Narrative World — KAIJU & MOVIE Format
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: The KAIJU and MOVIE tokens deliver the second-best cost per result in the account at scale, with notably high CTR (3.125% and 3.325% respectively). These tokens suggest a cinematic, world-building creative angle that resonates strongly at TOFU. This pillar tests whether a narrative/story-driven format — presenting the belt as part of a larger aesthetic universe rather than as a product — consistently outperforms utilitarian product formats.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: KAIJU: 30 results, CPA $14.96, CTR 3.125%, 32 unique ads, $448.88 spend. MOVIE: 27 results, CPA $14.98, CTR 3.325%, only 2 unique ads — highest result-per-ad efficiency in the dataset at 13.5 results per ad. DROP STATIC: 2 results, CPA $9.83, CTR 6.25% (8 unique ads, $19.66 spend — very low spend, directional only). MORETHANJUSTAWALLET: 2 results, CPA $31.22, CTR 6.25% (5 unique ads, $62.44 — low spend). SKULLSADONFLOOR at 53 results/$23.38 CPA is the highest-volume token but CTR of 1.347% and higher CPA suggest it converts but does not thumb-stop efficiently.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU brand-world immersion. The narrative format introduces the product through aesthetic identity rather than feature-benefit logic. This is appropriate for audiences who are unaware of the brand and need cultural context before a purchase proposition.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: MOVIE token is 2 unique ads with 27 results — this is exceptional per-ad efficiency and must be expanded immediately into more creative variants. Cinematic framing, dramatic pacing, world-building copy. Avoid direct product comparisons (OFFBEATVSTEMU: 1 result, CPA $99.65, CTR 0.581% — the comparison angle fails badly). THEBELTISTHEFIT token (14 results, CPA $36.37) underperforms relative to the narrative tokens, suggesting product-centric copy weakens results when paired with this aesthetic.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Instagram Feed primary (dominates purchase rows in conversion data). Reels placement is viable for cinematic video formats — conversion_tracking shows Instagram Reels: 2 link clicks, 1 add-to-cart, 2 checkouts initiated, 1 purchase (strong funnel depth for limited volume).
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: MOVIE token at 2 unique ads is severely under-tested. Expand to 6–8 variants to validate whether the signal holds. KAIJU at 32 unique ads with sustained CPA $14.96 is more mature and should be the budget anchor while MOVIE variants are tested at lower spend.

message_pillars.label: Anti-Generic / Comparison Angle — Positioning Against Drop Culture & Commodity
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Tokens NO/TEMU and DROPSLOP suggest a creative angle that positions the brand explicitly against low-quality commodity products (Temu, fast-fashion drops). Despite moderate CTR, these generate results at competitive CPAs and tap into audience identity — the target customer likely self-identifies as someone who rejects generic accessories. This pillar tests whether leaning into the anti-commodity identity angle at MOFU/BOFU improves cost per result among warmer audiences.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: NO/TEMU (shared unique_ads=1): 13 results each, CPA $28.84, CTR 2.648%, $374.98 spend. DROPSLOP: 13 results, CPA $31.63, CTR 2.425%, $411.13 spend — 2 unique ads. OFFBEATVSTEMU: 1 result, CPA $99.65, CTR 0.581% — the explicit comparison ad format failed badly (1 unique ad, $99.65 spend), suggesting the angle works better implicitly (as brand identity signal) than as a direct head-to-head comparison. THEBELTISTHEFIT: 14 results, CPA $36.37, CTR 1.443% — underperforms, implying direct product-first copy doesn't carry this angle effectively.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU primary, BOFU secondary. Audiences who have already seen brand-world content (Pillar 1 or 2) and are evaluating whether this brand is worth it over cheaper alternatives. The hook acknowledges the problem (generic belts, drop culture disappointment) before presenting the brand as the solution.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Do NOT use explicit side-by-side product comparisons — OFFBEATVSTEMU failed at $99.65 CPA. Instead, use implicit positioning: copy and visuals that signal 'this is not that' without naming competitors directly. The TEMU token success ($28.84 CPA) suggests the word or concept alone in copy is sufficient. Test whether the anti-generic hook in copy alone (without visual comparison) maintains the CPA advantage.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Instagram Feed is the dominant purchase-completion placement across conversion data. Facebook Feed contributed checkouts (3 checkouts, 1 purchase in platform data) and is worth retaining in Advantage+ rotation at this funnel stage.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Low-confidence pillar at current sample sizes (13 results each from 1–2 unique ads for the top tokens). Needs 4–6 new variants to generate readable signal before budget concentration. Flag as medium priority until sample matures.

message_pillars.label: Handcraft & Origin Story — Maker Identity and Material Proof
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Tokens HANDMADE, CUT1, and the UGC/maker-adjacent tokens (GRIFFREPLACEBELTUGC, FRANKIEVID) point toward a craft-origin narrative angle. CUT1 has the second-highest CTR in the dataset (4.615%, CPA $13.45) despite only 1 unique ad. HANDMADE delivers competitive CPA ($20.32, 2 results, 13 unique ads). This pillar tests whether a founder/maker story or raw craft demonstration (cutting, stitching, material close-up) outperforms polished lifestyle formats among audiences motivated by authenticity and anti-mass-production values.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: CUT1: 6 results, CPA $13.45, CTR 4.615%, 1 unique ad, $80.71 spend — extremely high CTR but single-ad signal, treat as directional. HANDMADE: 2 results, CPA $20.32, CTR 1.724%, 13 unique ads, $40.64 spend — low absolute results but consistent token appearance. GRIFFREPLACEBELTUGC: 4 results, CPA $34.18, CTR 1.408% — UGC with replacement/comparison framing underperforms on CPA. FRANKIEVID: 2 results, CPA $35.60, CTR 1.515% — video UGC underperforms the icon/sigil formats. WALLET: 2 results, CPA $50.62, CTR 0.909% — worst-performing adjacent token, suggesting product-photo-of-accessory framing without craft context fails.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU brand introduction and MOFU trust-building. The craft-origin hook functions as both a thumbstop (process video, material texture) and a trust signal (this is made by a real person with real skill). Feeds into BOFU when paired with social proof or review tokens.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Prioritise process video over finished-product shots — CUT1 (cutting process, 4.615% CTR) dramatically outperforms PRODUCTPHOTOBELTS (1 result, CPA $145.52, CTR 0.467%) and BELTS (16 results, CPA $31.28, CTR 1.148%). Maker-to-camera or hands-in-frame formats are preferred over polished studio shots. REVIEW token (4 results, CPA $23.58, CTR 2.740%) suggests review-as-proof copy can be integrated into this pillar at MOFU.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. iPhone is the dominant device in conversion tracking (majority of add-to-cart and purchase rows are iPhone). Ensure creative is vertical-native for Instagram Feed and Stories. Stories placement drove 1 purchase with 9 link clicks (reasonable funnel depth) and is worth including for craft/process content.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: CUT1 is the most urgent expansion target — 1 unique ad with 6 results and 4.615% CTR is an unvalidated anomaly that needs 4–6 variant expansions immediately. If the signal holds across 5+ ads, this becomes the primary creative direction for the account.

active_hypotheses.source: REDSIGILCLOSEUP token cluster — static sigil close-up format
active_hypotheses.risk: PINKSIGILREEL's advantage may be confounded by copy or CTA differences rather than the motion format alone. Single-variable isolation will clarify this. If motion underperforms, the static format is confirmed as the canonical sigil treatment.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Animated or looping motion version of the same sigil/icon asset, matched on copy and CTA, differing only in static vs. motion format
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: CN_ProductDemo format sub-type: static image (control) vs. motion/reel (variant). Distributed as: static sigil held constant in C1A and C3A (two different ICP columns, same row); motion sigil held constant in C2A and C4A (two different ICP columns, same row). The variable appears in exactly 2 cells per format type across 4 different avatar contexts — readable per IAP golden rule.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: Motion sigil variant achieves cost per result ≤ $14.00 (matching PINKSIGILREEL benchmark) vs. static control ≥ $20.00 (REDSIGILCLOSEUP baseline) across a minimum of 20 results per cell before verdict.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High — a confirmed 30%+ CPA advantage for motion sigil would redirect creative production investment and establish the animation direction for all future brand-icon assets.

active_hypotheses.label: Expanding the MOVIE token from 2 unique ads to 6+ variants will confirm or refute whether the cinematic/narrative format ($14.98 CPA, 3.325% CTR, 27 results from 2 ads) is a genuine format advantage or a lucky small-sample outlier.

active_hypotheses.label: An implicit anti-commodity positioning hook in copy (referencing 'Temu' or 'drop slop' as a contrast, without direct visual comparison) will achieve lower cost per result than an explicit side-by-side comparison creative, because OFFBEATVSTEMU (explicit comparison: $99.65 CPA, CTR 0.581%) dramatically underperforms NO/TEMU (implicit: $28.84 CPA, CTR 2.648%).
active_hypotheses.source: OFFBEATVSTEMU token — explicit visual comparison ad format ($99.65 CPA, 1 result, 1 unique ad)

Implicit variant appears in C3B and C4B (2 cells, 2 different avatar columns). If implicit copy alone achieves sub-$25 CPA without a comparison visual, it confirms that identity-signal copy is sufficient and comparison creative should be retired permanently.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium — resolves the comparison vs. identity-signal question definitively, protecting future creative budget from the explicit comparison trap ($99.65 CPA).

active_hypotheses.label: A raw process/craft video hook (cutting, stitching, material handling — CUT1 style at 4.615% CTR) will outperform a finished-product static image (PRODUCTPHOTOBELTS: CTR 0.467%, CPA $145.52) on both CTR and cost per result, confirming that process-revelation is a superior thumbstop format for this brand.

active_hypotheses.test_variant: 4 CUT1-style process video variants: hands in frame, raw material handling, cutting or stitching action in first 2 seconds. Varied across TN_Warm / TN_Relatable / FW_BAB / FW_StoryBrand. Held in column C4 (exploratory ICP column) rows A through D.

If CTR is high but cost per result fails to improve, a landing-page or post-click issue is flagged for investigation.

active_hypotheses.label: Adding a social proof or review copy element (REVIEW token: $23.58 CPA, CTR 2.740%) to a high-performing visual format (sigil or cinematic) will improve cost per result at MOFU compared to the same visual without proof copy, because the REVIEW token's CPA and CTR suggest proof-layer copy adds conversion value without hurting thumbstop.
