icp_profiles.message_resonance: Sigil/brand icon formats (PINKSIGILREEL $9.78 CPA, REDSIGILCLOSEUP $20.69 CPA), cinematic world-building (KAIJU $14.96 CPA, MOVIE $14.98 CPA), and implicit anti-commodity copy (NO/TEMU $28.84 CPA) all resonate. Explicit comparison formats fail (OFFBEATVSTEMU $99.65 CPA). Assertive and aspirational tonality works; warm/relatable is secondary. Process/craft hooks (CUT1 4.615% CTR) are a strong directional signal for this ICP's authenticity values.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: This ICP engages with aesthetically distinctive content (high CTR on sigil/icon close-ups, cinematic formats) rather than catalog or product-grid layouts (CATALOG: $97.87 CPA, PRODUCTPHOTOBELTS: $145.52 CPA). They click through on curiosity hooks and brand-world content before converting. Funnel depth is moderate — conversion_tracking shows Instagram Feed as the dominant purchase-completion environment, suggesting this ICP browses and converts within a single session rather than requiring extended retargeting. Price sensitivity appears low relative to the account's CPA range ($9–$37 cost per result suggests a higher-ticket item where identity alignment drives conversion more than price objection.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU via brand-world or icon-led creative on Instagram Feed or Reels. They are AW_Unaware at entry — they've never heard of the brand — and respond to curiosity and aesthetic distinction before any product explanation is needed.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: Core identity is built around rejecting mass-produced, algorithm-driven fashion drops. This person is actively aware of 'drop culture' and its commodification — they know what Temu is, they've bought disappointing fast-fashion belts or accessories before, and they're looking for something that signals genuine taste and craft knowledge. The brand's anti-Temu and DROPSLOP token performance ($28.84 CPA and $31.63 CPA respectively) suggests this identity resonance is real. They're not primarily price-sensitive — they're quality-and-identity sensitive. The WALLET token's failure ($50.62 CPA) suggests they're not motivated by accessory completeness or utility framing.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Likely skews 18–34, mobile-first (iPhone dominant per conversion_tracking device data — majority of add-to-cart and purchase rows are iPhone), Instagram-native. Geography is unconfirmed from the evidence but POST AUS/NZ token (2 results, $18.84 CPA, CTR 2.5%) suggests an English-speaking Southern Hemisphere segment is present and cost-competitive. Broad targeting, no demographic micro-targeting warranted under Andromeda ABO context.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Anchor Column C1 of the Matrix Sprint Test to this ICP. Lead with sigil/icon motion creative (PINKSIGILREEL style) at TOFU, sequence into cinematic narrative (MOVIE/KAIJU style) at MOFU, and close with implicit anti-commodity copy at BOFU. Do not use catalog or product-photo formats for this ICP — the evidence is unambiguous that they underperform.

icp_profiles.message_resonance: Process video hooks (CUT1 4.615% CTR), HANDMADE copy token ($20.32 CPA), and FounderStory or BAB frameworks are directionally strong. Warm and relatable tonality (TN_Warm, TN_Relatable) suits this ICP better than assertive or aspirational. REVIEW token ($23.58 CPA, 2.740% CTR) as a MOFU proof layer is plausible for this segment. Polished product photography (PRODUCTPHOTOBELTS $145.52 CPA) is actively harmful for this ICP.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: High thumbstop response to process/action hooks — CUT1's 4.615% CTR is the second-highest in the dataset and comes from a process-video format. This ICP likely pauses on unexpected visual content (hands working on leather, cutting motions) rather than static imagery. Funnel conversion data is thin for craft-specific tokens but HANDMADE at $20.32 CPA across 13 unique ads (only 2 results) suggests the format attracts clicks but conversion to result needs copy optimisation. This ICP may require a MOFU touchpoint (proof or review layer) before converting.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU via process video or craft-reveal hook. AW_Unaware at entry — responds to 'how is this made' before 'what is this brand.' MOFU requires a trust bridge (maker story, material proof, or review layer) before BOFU conversion.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: Motivated by the story of how things are made. This person responds to process revelation — watching a craftsperson cut, shape, or finish a piece is more compelling than seeing the finished product in a studio setting. CUT1 (process cut video, 4.615% CTR, $13.45 CPA) and HANDMADE token ($20.32 CPA) both directionally support this profile. The FRANKIEVID UGC token underperforms ($35.60 CPA) while the raw process token outperforms, suggesting this ICP responds to maker authenticity over polished UGC testimonial. They value origin, material, and skill — not social proof from strangers.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Mobile-first, Instagram-native, likely skews 22–38. No demographic breakdown is available in the evidence (demographic_signal array is empty), so age and gender are inferred from psychographic signals only. iPhone and Android split is roughly 60/40 in conversion_tracking device data — this ICP likely spans both. Geography unknown; treat as broad under Andromeda execution.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Assign this ICP to Column C4 as an exploratory expansion column in the Matrix Sprint Test. Prioritise expanding CUT1 into 4 variants (Hypothesis 4) within this column. If the process-video CTR advantage holds across 4+ ads, this ICP profile graduates from exploratory to validated and warrants its own dedicated budget allocation.

icp_profiles.message_resonance: Motion-first, sound-on creative (PINKSIGILREEL style). Fast cuts, visual surprise, minimal copy. Assertive or playful tonality. The hook must land in 1–2 seconds. SKULLSADONFLOOR (53 results, $23.38 CPA) may partially overlap this ICP given its high result volume — worth testing whether the skulls visual asset was primarily Reels-delivered.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: Converts fast — 2 link clicks produced 2 checkouts and 1 purchase in the Reels placement row, suggesting near-zero consideration gap. This is atypical and may reflect an unusually motivated micro-cohort or algorithm-delivered perfect-fit audience. The signal is too thin (2 link clicks) to be reliable but warrants a dedicated Reels-format test. Price sensitivity appears very low — impulse conversion at this speed suggests the price point is not a barrier.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU directly into BOFU — this ICP may not require a traditional MOFU touchpoint. They see → click → buy in a single session via Reels.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: This ICP discovers and converts within the Reels environment — they are not browse-and-deliberate buyers. They respond to fast-paced, visually striking content that creates immediate desire without requiring research. The PINKSIGILREEL token ($9.78 CPA, motion format) and the Reels placement's high funnel depth ratio are mutually reinforcing — motion, rhythm, and visual surprise drive impulsive funnel progression. They are unlikely to be motivated by long-form copy, comparison framing, or catalog-style layouts. HK_Curiosity and HK_Benefit hooks work; HK_Problem hooks may be too slow for this attention window.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Mobile-first, Instagram Reels primary placement, likely skews 18–28. Conversion_tracking shows Instagram Reels: 2 link clicks, 1 add-to-cart, 2 checkouts initiated, 1 purchase — an extremely high funnel depth ratio for the volume (50% checkout rate, 50% purchase rate from link clicks). This is a thin but provocative signal. iPhone-dominant based on overall device data. Broad geographic targeting under Andromeda.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Assign this ICP to Column C3 as a semi-exploratory column. Test Reels-native creative (vertical, sound-on, sub-2-second hook) as the column constant, with the ICP designation as 'Reels Impulse Converter.' Monitor Advantage+ placement breakdown for Reels delivery. If Reels-delivered cost per result consistently beats Feed for the same creative, advocate for Reels-specific asset production investment.

message_pillars.label: Static Image Efficiency — Lead Gen Volume Engine
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Static image creatives are the account's dominant cost-per-qualified-lead driver. The top-performing individual ads are all static JPG/PNG formats achieving cost per qualified lead between $1.28 and $2.39, while video formats (V3.mp4, V4.mp4, VID) average $8.85–$17.24 per qualified lead. This pillar systematically exploits the static image advantage by testing which visual hook, offer frame, and copy angle compounds efficiency gains at scale. The objective is exclusively lead_gen — cost per qualified lead is the terminal metric.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: ChatGPT Image Jul 31 PNG: 720 leads, $1.28 cost per qualified lead, 64.6% CVR from link click. STAT_01.JPG token: 758 leads, $1.95 cost per qualified lead, 58.6% CVR. STAT_02.JPG token: 883 leads, $2.39 cost per qualified lead, 41.7% CVR. STAT_FREETRAINING_01.jpg: 446 leads, $1.71 cost per qualified lead, 59.1% CVR. STAT_FREE_04.jpg: 204 leads, $1.67 cost per qualified lead, 51.6% CVR. STAT_PERFECTPOUT_04.jpg: 34 leads, $1.28 cost per qualified lead, 64.2% CVR. STAT_ESCAPE_10.jpg: 109 leads, $1.64 cost per qualified lead, 38.8% CVR. In contrast, V3.mp4: $17.24 cost per qualified lead, 16.0% CVR; V4.mp4: $10.36 cost per qualified lead, 22.8% CVR. Facebook Feed is the strongest placement (2,581 results, $4.11 cost per result) followed by Instagram Feed (1,763 results, $4.85 cost per result). Primary audience is females 35–54 at $5.05–$5.16 cost per qualified lead; females 25–34 achieve $4.45 and females 18–24 achieve $2.43.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU and MOFU static image ads driving form leads directly. The high link-click-to-lead CVR (40–65%) on top performers indicates the form page is well-matched to creative promise — maintain offer consistency between ad and landing form.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: All creatives in this pillar are static JPG or PNG. Test offer-word hooks (FREETRAINING, DREAMCAREER, ESCAPE, PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES) as the primary variable across rows. Keep the STAT_ design system constant within concept columns. CTA family fixed per column. Advantage+ auto-placements active — Facebook Feed and Instagram Feed will capture the majority of delivery based on placement CPA evidence.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Do not restrict placements — Facebook Feed ($4.11 CPA) and Instagram Feed ($4.85 CPA) will self-optimize. Facebook Reels ($8.73 CPA) and Stories ($7.01–$8.89 CPA) will receive incidental delivery; monitor but do not suppress during the test window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Scale winning static image variants via budget increase on ABO sets once a creative achieves 50+ leads and cost per qualified lead at or below account average ($4.04 blended). Do not scale video creative alongside static in the same ad set — isolate format advantage. Prioritize the ChatGPT-generated PNG style (AI-generated imagery) as a distinct design system to test against the STAT_ photo design system.

message_pillars.label: Offer-Word Hook Testing — Keyword-Driven Lead Intent Signal
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: The variable_performance data reveals that specific offer-word tokens in ad names produce dramatically different cost per qualified lead outcomes under the lead_gen objective. Tokens like DREAMCAREER ($1.64 CPL, 39.4% CVR), ESCAPE ($1.52 CPL, 45.7% CVR), PERFECTPOUT ($2.23 CPL, 54.8% CVR), FIXFROWNLINES ($2.97 CPL, 56.8% CVR), and FREETRAINING ($2.13 CPL, 54.0% CVR) outperform generic tokens like VID ($8.85 CPL), INJECT ($6.67 CPL), LOUIS ($10.73 CPL), JACKET ($13.03 CPL), and V3/V4 video files ($10.41–$17.24 CPL). This pillar isolates the copy hook angle as the primary variable to determine whether the offer word itself (aspirational career/lifestyle vs. aesthetic treatment vs. generic descriptor) is driving the lead-quality and volume gap.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: ESCAPE token: 323 leads across 68 ads, $1.52 cost per qualified lead, 45.7% CVR. DREAMCAREER token: 600 leads across 64 ads, $1.64 cost per qualified lead, 39.4% CVR. PERFECTPOUT token: 211 leads across 67 ads, $2.22 cost per qualified lead, 54.8% CVR. FIXFROWNLINES token: 297 leads across 42 ads, $2.97 cost per qualified lead, 56.8% CVR. FREETRAINING token: 657 leads across 155 ads, $2.13 cost per qualified lead, 54.0% CVR. FREE token: 641 leads across 116 ads, $3.37 cost per qualified lead, 36.8% CVR. Compare to JACKET: 1,050 leads across 92 ads, $13.03 cost per qualified lead, 19.4% CVR — highest volume but worst efficiency. LOUIS: 291 leads, $10.73 cost per qualified lead, 23.4% CVR. SUMM: 157 leads, $11.38 cost per qualified lead, 23.4% CVR. The STAT_ (4,111 leads, $4.04 CPL) token aggregate shows static format carries significant weight, but within static the offer-word determines the efficiency tier.
message_pillars.funnel_application: Primarily TOFU lead capture. High-performing offer words (ESCAPE, DREAMCAREER, PERFECTPOUT) appear to serve both career-aspirant and aesthetic-outcome audiences — the matrix should test these hooks against distinct ICPs to determine if hook-ICP fit explains the variance or if the hook itself is universally superior.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Each matrix row tests one offer-word hook family held constant across all four concept columns (ICP avatars). The hook is the isolated variable per row. Design system (CN_Design_STAT for columns C1–C3; exploratory design for C4) and CTA remain fixed within columns. Do not mix aspirational career hooks (DREAMCAREER, ESCAPE) with aesthetic treatment hooks (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES, PEPTIDE) within the same row — this conflates two different hook categories and destroys isolation. Aspirational career hooks map to Row A; treatment outcome hooks map to Row B; free-offer hooks (FREETRAINING, FREE) map to Row C; problem-pain hooks (STOPCHASING, FIXFROWNLINES) map to Row D.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Hook-level differences will be readable across placements given the volume of leads generated in the account. Monitor CTR and CVR separately — a hook may drive high CTR but low CVR (indicating curiosity without intent) or low CTR with high CVR (indicating self-qualifying behavior).
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: After 100+ leads per hook variant, rank by cost per qualified lead within each ICP column. Hooks that win in 2+ columns are column-agnostic winners and should be carried into the next sprint at higher budget. Hooks that win in only one column are ICP-specific and should be deepened in that column only.

message_pillars.label: Video vs. AI-Generated Static Format Test — Format Efficiency Isolation
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: The account shows a persistent and large format performance gap under the lead_gen objective. Video formats (V3.mp4, V4.mp4, VID, LOUIS video, OLD.mp4) consistently produce cost per qualified lead of $4.55–$17.24 and CVR of 15–30% from link click. The highest-performing creative in the account is the AI-generated ChatGPT PNG (720 leads, $1.28 CPL, 64.6% CVR) followed by the 8.4 gen.mp4 video ($1.88 CPL, 49.2% CVR — the single video exception). This pillar tests whether the AI-generated visual style itself (rather than static vs. video as a binary) is the confounding variable driving the ChatGPT PNG's outsized performance. The 8.4 gen.mp4 — the only video near static efficiency — may share visual characteristics with the AI-generated image style.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: ChatGPT Image Jul 31 PNG: $1.28 cost per qualified lead, 720 leads, 64.6% link-click CVR, $919 spend. 8.4 gen.mp4: $1.88 cost per qualified lead, 327 leads, 49.2% CVR, $615 spend (only 12 unique ads — low confidence, validation_required). Jacket_V4.mp4: $10.36 CPL, 607 leads, 22.8% CVR, $6,288 spend. Jacket_V3.mp4: $17.14 CPL, 305 leads, 15.9% CVR, $5,228 spend. VID token: $8.85 CPL, 538 leads, 24.4% CVR. OLD.mp4: $4.55 CPL, 180 leads, 30.3% CVR. Sydney Nurses 2.mp4: $2.58 CPL, 74 leads, 44.0% CVR (small sample, low confidence). Facebook Reels placement (likely absorbing video spend): $8.73 CPL vs. Facebook Feed $4.11 CPL. The JACKET video token alone accounts for $13,682 spend at $13.03 CPL — representing a significant efficiency drag on the account.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU format test. If the AI-generated image style proves superior to both traditional static and video, it should become the default design system for all lead gen columns. If 8.4 gen.mp4 (AI-generated video) replicates the PNG's efficiency, a mixed-format AI creative approach is warranted. This test resolves format allocation for the next 2–3 sprints.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Test four format variants within the same hook and ICP: (1) AI-generated static PNG (control, ChatGPT-style image), (2) AI-generated short video/animated (8.4 gen.mp4 style), (3) traditional static photo (STAT_ design system), (4) traditional video (best-performing traditional video as baseline). Hold hook word, offer, and CTA constant across all four format variants. This is a single-variable test with format as the isolated variable. Note: the 8.4 gen.mp4 has only 12 unique ads in the dataset — treat its $1.88 CPL as low-confidence and requiring validation before budget commitment.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Video variants will naturally receive more Reels/Stories delivery; do not suppress this — the test measures real-world format performance including placement distribution effects. Report CPL by format at the end of the sprint, not by placement.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Maintain equal starting budgets across format variants within each ABO set. Do not manually boost the AI-generated PNG based on historical data — let the sprint generate fresh comparable data. If AI PNG again achieves CPL below $2.00 with 100+ leads, shift 60% of creative budget to AI-generated image production for the following sprint.

message_pillars.label: Geographic and Treatment-Specific Angle Isolation — Local Signal Test
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: The account contains ad names with explicit city/geography tokens (ATL, CLE, DEN, CHI, LV, NYC, DAL, SCO) applied to both injection/treatment ads and enrollment ads. These geo-specific variants consistently underperform the best non-geo static creatives: ATL_INJECT_2: $6.78 CPL; CLE_INJECT_1: $4.80 CPL; LV_INJECT_2: $7.94 CPL; DEN_INJECT_1: $6.75 CPL; CHI_INJECT_1: $7.09 CPL; vs. non-geo STAT_ESCAPE: $1.52–$1.75 CPL. However, these geo ads are running under broad Advantage+ targeting, which may undermine the geographic specificity intended. This pillar tests whether the geo angle itself (local relevance) vs. the treatment-specific content (INJECT) is the driver of underperformance — and whether removing geography while keeping treatment specificity improves results.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: INJECT token: 422 leads across 608 ads, $6.67 cost per qualified lead, 26.9% CVR. ATL token: 144 leads, $6.66 CPL. CLE token: 157 leads, $6.04 CPL. SUMM token: 157 leads, $11.38 CPL, 23.4% CVR. FIXFROWNLINES (treatment-specific, no geo): 297 leads, $2.97 CPL, 56.8% CVR. PERFECTPOUT (treatment-specific, no geo): 211 leads, $2.22 CPL, 54.8% CVR. PEPTIDE (treatment-specific, no geo): 173 leads, $2.09 CPL, 61.8% CVR. The pattern is consistent: treatment-specific hooks without geographic qualifiers achieve 2–3x lower CPL and 2x higher CVR than geo-tagged treatment ads.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU test for treatment-seeking leads. If geo-removal alone lifts CVR toward the 50%+ range seen in non-geo treatment hooks, this confirms that broad Advantage+ targeting with geo-qualified copy creates audience-message mismatch. The implication is that geo-specific campaigns require geo-constrained targeting — which conflicts with the Andromeda broad-targeting execution context and should be retired in favor of universal treatment-hook copy.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Row A: geo-tagged treatment copy (control — current state, e.g. ATL_INJECT). Row B: treatment-hook copy without geo (e.g. FIXFROWNLINES, PERFECTPOUT). Row C: treatment-hook copy with outcome framing (PEPTIDE, PERFECTPOUT) — outcome-first vs. pain-first. Row D: social proof or testimonial frame on same treatment hook. Design system and CTA held constant within each column/ICP. Geographic removal is the isolated variable in Row A vs. Row B.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Do not add geographic targeting constraints — this would confound the test by changing the targeting variable simultaneously with the copy variable. The test must run broad to isolate copy angle only.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: If non-geo treatment hooks achieve CPL at least 30% lower than geo-tagged equivalents after 80+ leads per variant, retire all geo-tagged copy from the lead gen rotation and redirect budget to universal treatment-hook static creatives. Flag the geographic angle as low-confidence for broad-targeting campaigns.

active_hypotheses.label: Replacing the JACKET video creative (current highest-spend video, $13.03 cost per qualified lead, 19.4% CVR) with an AI-generated static PNG using an equivalent aspirational hook will reduce cost per qualified lead by at least 40% within the lead_gen objective.
active_hypotheses.source: Jacket_V4.mp4 / Jacket_V3.mp4 — combined $11,517 spend, blended ~$13–17 cost per qualified lead
active_hypotheses.risk: The JACKET video may carry audience-building or brand-awareness value not captured in lead count alone. If the video drives downstream lead quality (e.g. higher close rate on calls), the CPL improvement in-platform may not translate to better business outcomes. Additionally, the ChatGPT PNG's historical performance ($1.28 CPL) may not replicate at higher budget — the original ran on only $919 spend.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: AI-generated PNG creative (ChatGPT/generative image style) carrying the same aspirational career/lifestyle hook as the JACKET video, served under identical broad targeting and Advantage+ placements in an ABO set alongside the video control.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: Creative format: AI-generated static PNG vs. traditional video. Distributed across the matrix as the column-constant design system variable — C1 holds CN_Design_AIGeneratedPNG constant across rows A–D; C2 holds CN_Design_TraditionalVideo constant across rows A–D. Hook, offer, CTA, and ICP are identical across C1 and C2 to ensure format is the only variable. This gives 4 format comparisons (one per row) across 4 different hook angles, satisfying the 2–4 appearance rule for the format variable.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: AI-generated PNG achieves cost per qualified lead ≤ $7.80 (40% below the JACKET video blended CPL of $13.03) with a minimum of 100 leads generated within the sprint window. Secondary signal: link-click CVR ≥ 35% vs. JACKET video's 19–23% range.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High — the JACKET video represents the account's largest single spend efficiency drain ($11,517 at $13–17 CPL). Even a 30% CPL improvement on this budget allocation would save approximately $3,500–$5,000 per sprint cycle and redirect it to proven sub-$2 CPL static formats.

active_hypotheses.label: Aspirational career/escape hooks (DREAMCAREER, ESCAPE) will outperform aesthetic treatment hooks (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES) on cost per qualified lead for the career-aspirant ICP audience, while the reverse will hold for the aesthetic consumer ICP — confirming that hook-ICP fit, not hook type alone, drives efficiency.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 2 offer-word evidence: ESCAPE at $1.52 CPL and DREAMCAREER at $1.64 CPL (aggregate, not ICP-separated); PERFECTPOUT at $2.22 CPL and FIXFROWNLINES at $2.97 CPL (aggregate)
active_hypotheses.risk: With broad Advantage+ targeting and no ICP-level audience constraints, the 'ICP columns' are concept-level isolations (avatar-defined by creative content and design), not true demographic segments. Meta may optimize delivery similarly across columns, reducing the ICP isolation fidelity. Treat column-level learnings as directional hypotheses requiring a second-sprint confirmation.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Matrix rows A and B each hold one hook family constant across all four columns (ICP avatars). Row A: aspirational career hook (DREAMCAREER or ESCAPE) applied to all four ICPs. Row B: aesthetic treatment hook (PERFECTPOUT or FIXFROWNLINES) applied to all four ICPs. The cross-column CPL pattern reveals whether hook performance is ICP-dependent or universal.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: Hook angle family (aspirational career vs. aesthetic treatment), held constant within each row and varied across rows. Each hook family appears in exactly 4 cells (one per column), satisfying the 2–4 distribution rule. All other variables — design system, CTA, tone, format — are held constant within columns. The interaction effect (hook × ICP) is readable by comparing row-level CPL within each column.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: A statistically interpretable pattern where at least 2 of 4 ICP columns show ≥20% CPL difference between Row A and Row B, with the direction of advantage differing across ICP columns. Minimum 50 leads per cell before reading. If all four columns show the same hook winning, the hook is audience-agnostic (simplifying future creative strategy).
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium — clarifies whether creative strategy should be ICP-differentiated (requiring 4 distinct creative tracks) or hook-universal (allowing one winning hook family to serve all columns). If hooks are universal, this simplifies production and concentrates budget on fewer proven concepts.

active_hypotheses.label: Removing geographic qualifiers from treatment-specific ad copy (replacing ATL/CLE/DEN/CHI/LV geo-tagged variants with universal treatment hooks like FIXFROWNLINES or PEPTIDE) will reduce cost per qualified lead by at least 50% under broad Advantage+ targeting.
active_hypotheses.source: Geo-tagged INJECT ads: STAT_ATL_INJECT_2 ($6.78 CPL), STAT_LV_INJECT_2 ($7.94 CPL), STAT_DEN_INJECT_1 ($6.75 CPL), STAT_CHI_INJECT_1 ($7.09 CPL) — blended ~$7.00 CPL
active_hypotheses.risk: If geo-tagged ads are actually driving higher-quality leads (more likely to attend in-person appointments in specific cities), removing geo specificity may increase lead volume but reduce downstream conversion to booked appointments. This test measures in-platform CPL only — recommend tracking lead-to-appointment rate offline before retiring geo-tagged creatives entirely.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: STAT_ design system static image carrying FIXFROWNLINES or PEPTIDE hook with no geographic qualifier, served under the same broad Advantage+ targeting and ABO budget as the geo-tagged control ads.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: Presence of geographic qualifier in ad copy (geo-tagged vs. universal hook). Held constant within Row A (geo control) and Row B (universal hook test) of the matrix, varied across rows. Appears in 4 cells per treatment (one per column/ICP), satisfying the 2–4 distribution rule. Design system (STAT_), format (static PNG/JPG), CTA, and ICP column are held constant to isolate the geographic copy variable only.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: Universal treatment hook achieves cost per qualified lead ≤ $3.50 (50% below geo-tagged blended $7.00 CPL) with minimum 80 leads per variant within the sprint window. CVR from link click should exceed 45% for the universal hook vs. the geo-tagged ads' ~27% baseline.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium-high — if confirmed, this finding would retire a family of underperforming creatives consuming budget at $6.75–$7.94 CPL and redirect to universal treatment hooks proven at $2.09–$2.97 CPL. The INJECT token alone spans 608 unique ads and $2,816 spend at $6.67 CPL — a meaningful efficiency opportunity.

active_hypotheses.label: The AI-generated chatbot-style image format (ChatGPT PNG aesthetic) will sustain its $1.28–$1.88 cost per qualified lead efficiency when scaled from $919–$923 historical spend to $3,000+ sprint budget, or will show diminishing returns above a spend threshold.
active_hypotheses.source: ChatGPT Image Jul 31 PNG: $919 spend, 720 leads, $1.28 CPL, 64.6% CVR — single ad, 27 unique ad variants in token group
active_hypotheses.risk: High recency bias risk — the ChatGPT PNG ran in July–August 2026 with limited budget; its exceptional CPL may reflect audience novelty with the AI-generated aesthetic rather than a structural creative advantage. The 8.4 gen.mp4 ($1.88 CPL, only 12 unique ads) is similarly thin evidence. Both should be treated as validation_required until replicated at scale.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: 3–4 new AI-generated static PNG creatives in the same visual style, each carrying a different tested hook (DREAMCAREER, PERFECTPOUT, FREETRAINING, ESCAPE), run at $750–$1,000 ABO budget each to build volume while testing hook variation within the format.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: Budget scale and hook variation within the AI-generated PNG format. The format (CN_Design_AIGeneratedPNG) is held constant as the column constant for C1 across all rows A–D. The hook angle (HK_Benefit, HK_Problem, HK_Curiosity, HK_Story) varies across rows A–D. This tests both the format's scalability and the hook-within-format interaction. Each hook appears once in C1, once in another column with a different design system — meeting the 2-appearance minimum for hook isolation.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: At least 2 of 4 AI-generated PNG variants achieve cost per qualified lead ≤ $2.50 at $750+ spend each. If CPL inflates above $4.00 at scale for all variants, the original ad's performance is attributed to novelty or a one-time audience match rather than repeatable format advantage. Thumbstop rate and CTR are the earliest readable signals before CPL stabilizes.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High if validated — establishing AI-generated imagery as a reliably superior design system would transform creative production strategy (lower cost, faster iteration) while delivering the account's lowest CPL tier. If not validated at scale, reallocates budget away from an untested format hypothesis.

active_hypotheses.label: A testimonial or social-proof hook (PR_Testimonial or PR_SocialProof) applied to the FREETRAINING or DREAMCAREER offer frame will outperform the current direct benefit-hook approach on cost per qualified lead for the females 35–54 core demographic, by increasing trust and reducing objection friction at MOFU.
active_hypotheses.source: STAT_FREETRAINING_01.jpg: $1.71 CPL, 446 leads, 59.1% CVR — current best FREETRAINING static; DREAMCAREER token: $1.64 CPL, 600 leads, 39.4% CVR
active_hypotheses.risk: Low evidence base for proof-layer performance — no current PR_Testimonial creatives are identifiable by name in the ad rollup data, so this is a net-new angle with no historical benchmark in this account. The test is exploratory. Females 35–54 account for the majority of leads (2,228 + 1,888 = 4,116 leads at $5.05–$5.16 CPL demographic average) but the demographic data is account-level aggregate, not creative-level, so ICP-specific response to proof cannot be confirmed from existing evidence.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Static image creative featuring a testimonial quote or real-student social proof overlay on the FREETRAINING or DREAMCAREER offer frame, matched to the STAT_ design system and same CTA family as the control.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: Proof mechanism layer: direct benefit hook (control) vs. social proof / testimonial overlay (variant). The proof variable (PR_Testimonial vs. PR_VisualDemo) is the sole variable changed. Appears in 2 cells in the matrix (one control row, one proof row) across 2+ different ICP columns to meet the 2–4 distribution rule and enable cross-avatar reading. All design, offer, format, and CTA elements remain constant.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: Testimonial/social-proof variant achieves cost per qualified lead ≤ $1.50 (beating the $1.71 FREETRAINING control) with minimum 150 leads, OR the control retains ≤ $2.00 CPL confirming the direct hook needs no proof layer at TOFU. Either outcome is a usable learning.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium — if proof layer improves the already-strong FREETRAINING creative, it opens a scalable social-proof production track. If it performs equivalently, confirms that direct benefit hooks are sufficient at TOFU and simplifies future creative briefs by removing testimonial production from the priority list.

active_hypotheses.label: A counter-diagonal variable isolation test — running HK_Curiosity hooks across cells C1D, C2C, C3B, C4A (each with a different ICP column design system) — will reveal whether curiosity-framed hooks generalize across all avatar types or are ICP-specific in their lead generation efficiency.
active_hypotheses.source: STAT_STOPCHASING: $3.91–$5.14 CPL with 142–164 leads — the closest existing curiosity/challenge hook in the account data; ESCAPE token ($1.52 CPL) provides a partial curiosity baseline
active_hypotheses.risk: The diagonal only produces 4 data points — volume per cell will be limited in a single sprint. Recommend a 3-week minimum sprint window or higher per-set budget to accumulate 40+ leads per diagonal cell. The design system varies across diagonal cells by design, which means CPL differences may reflect design rather than hook — this is intentional (diagonal tests generalizability, not purity) but must be interpreted accordingly.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Counter-diagonal (C1D, C2C, C3B, C4A) each carries HK_Curiosity as the shared angle variable, with each cell using its column's native design system (CN_Design_STAT for C1, CN_Design_AIGen for C2, CN_Design_UGC for C3, CN_Design_Exploratory for C4). The hook copy varies in surface wording per ICP but the curiosity mechanism (incomplete statement, implied revelation, 'what if' frame) is the constant.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_Curiosity hook mechanism, isolated on the counter-diagonal — appearing exactly 4 times across 4 different ICP columns and 4 different design systems, satisfying the diagonal isolation logic of the IAP MST methodology. All other row variables (tone, framework, stage) vary across diagonal cells. This is the highest-confidence signal position in the matrix — a variable winning on the diagonal has been tested across maximum diversity of contexts.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: HK_Curiosity achieves cost per qualified lead ≤ $3.00 in at least 3 of 4 diagonal cells with minimum 40 leads per cell. If curiosity hooks underperform direct benefit hooks (HK_Benefit) at comparable spend, the account's audience skews solution-aware or most-aware and does not respond to curiosity gap mechanics — a strategically important finding.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium — the diagonal test resolves one of the account's key unknowns: whether the audience is primarily problem-aware (responds to curiosity/pain hooks) or solution-aware (responds to direct benefit/offer hooks). This determines the hook strategy for the next 3+ sprint cycles.

icp_profiles.profile_name: Career-Transitioning Aesthetic Professional — The Dream Career Seeker
icp_profiles.message_resonance: Best resonance with: aspirational career/lifestyle hooks (DREAMCAREER, ESCAPE, STOPCHASING), direct benefit framing (HK_Benefit, FW_Direct), assertive or aspirational tone (TN_Assertive, TN_Aspirational), free-offer entry point (FREETRAINING, FREE), and static image format (STAT_ design system or AI-generated PNG). Weakest resonance with: geographic-specific copy (geo-inject ads average $6.75–$7.94 CPL vs. $1.52–$1.64 for universal hooks), video format (VID, JACKET video $8.85–$17 CPL), and treatment-specific aesthetic hooks (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES) which appear to attract a different ICP.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: Engages most strongly with static image creatives carrying career-aspiration copy — the DREAMCAREER token (600 leads, $1.64 CPL, 39.4% CVR) and ESCAPE token (323 leads, $1.52 CPL, 45.7% CVR) are the primary behavioral signals. The relatively lower CVR of DREAMCAREER (39.4%) vs. FREETRAINING (54–59%) suggests this ICP may be earlier in the decision funnel and requires a lower-friction entry point (free training vs. direct enrollment CTA). Sits at TOFU to early MOFU in the account's funnel. Price sensitivity is moderate — responds to 'free' offer framing as an entry point but the career-outcome aspiration implies willingness to invest once committed. Urgency response is moderate; does not appear to require scarcity mechanics based on available copy signals.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU via aspirational career hook on Facebook Feed or Instagram Feed static image, converting directly to form lead. The high CVR from link click (39–59%) suggests the landing form is well-matched to this ICP's intent level.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: This ICP is a professional or semi-professional woman in her late 20s to early 40s who is dissatisfied with her current career trajectory and is actively exploring adjacent industries that promise higher earnings, flexibility, or prestige. She is not primarily motivated by beauty outcomes for herself — she is motivated by the business or career opportunity that aesthetic services represent. Her core pain is feeling trapped (HP_Overwhelm, HP_Confidence) in a low-ceiling role and her aspiration is autonomy and income growth. She is solution-aware (AW_SolutionAware) — she knows training programs exist and is evaluating options. She responds to direct benefit framing and aspirational tone (TN_Aspirational) rather than problem-dwelling copy. Her decision style is research-oriented but form-completion behavior is fast once intent is confirmed, as evidenced by the 58–64% link-click CVR on FREETRAINING and DREAMCAREER top performers.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Females aged 25–44, with the 25–34 cohort achieving $4.45 cost per qualified lead and the 35–44 cohort at $5.05 CPL — both above the sub-$2 CPL seen in the best static creatives, suggesting the best performers are pulling from a subset within these age bands rather than the full demographic. Primarily engaged on Facebook Feed (best placement CPA at $4.11) and Instagram Feed ($4.85 CPA). Device and geography signals are not available at creative level in the current data (demographic report is account-aggregate at 98.8% spend coverage). The DREAMCAREER and ESCAPE offer tokens — which achieve $1.52–$1.64 CPL — suggest this ICP responds to copy about career change, financial freedom, and escaping a current situation rather than aesthetic treatment outcomes.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Build Concept Column C1 of the next Matrix Sprint Test exclusively around this ICP using the STAT_ or AI-generated PNG design system, DREAMCAREER/ESCAPE hook family in Row A, FREETRAINING in Row B, STOPCHASING in Row C, and a new aspirational story hook (HK_Story) in Row D. Keep CTA focused on free training or career discovery framing rather than appointment or treatment booking.

icp_profiles.profile_name: Aesthetic Treatment Consumer — The Outcome-Seeking Patient
icp_profiles.message_resonance: Best resonance with: treatment-specific outcome hooks naming the procedure or result (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES, PEPTIDE), direct problem-solution framing (FW_PAS, FW_Direct), confident assertive tone (TN_Assertive, TN_Warm), static STAT_ or AI-generated image design showing a before/after or treatment visual (PR_VisualDemo), and universal (non-geo) copy. Weakest resonance with: generic free-offer hooks without treatment specificity, video formats, and geographic qualifiers under broad targeting.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: PERFECTPOUT token: 211 leads, $2.22 CPL, 54.8% CVR across 67 ads. FIXFROWNLINES token: 297 leads, $2.97 CPL, 56.8% CVR across 42 ads. PEPTIDE token: 173 leads, $2.09 CPL, 61.8% CVR across 43 ads. STAT_PERFECTPOUT_04.jpg: $1.28 CPL, 34 leads, 64.2% CVR — among the account's top performers. STAT_FIXFROWNLINES_01.jpg: $2.24 CPL, 271 leads, 58.9% CVR. The treatment-specific hooks produce both high CVR and low CPL when delivered without geographic qualifiers. The geo-INJECT variants ($6.75–$7.94 CPL, ~27% CVR) serve what may be the same ICP but with geographic mismatch under broad targeting, explaining the CVR collapse.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: TOFU via treatment-specific outcome hook on Facebook Feed or Instagram Feed static image, converting directly to form lead (likely a consultation booking or free information request). The very high CVR (55–65% for top treatment hooks) confirms strong intent at point of click.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: This ICP is a woman in her late 30s to 60s who is actively seeking specific aesthetic treatments — lip filler, anti-wrinkle injections, peptide treatments — and is looking for a qualified provider or a free consultation to learn more. She is product/treatment-aware (AW_SolutionAware to AW_MostAware) and responds to treatment-specific copy that names her desired outcome precisely. Her core pain is HP_Confidence — she wants to look better and is actively researching. She is not primarily motivated by career outcomes. Her decision style is outcome-focused and she self-qualifies rapidly when the ad copy matches her specific treatment interest, producing the high CVR observed in PERFECTPOUT (54.8%), FIXFROWNLINES (56.8%), and PEPTIDE (61.8%) creatives.
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Females aged 35–64, with the 45–54 cohort (2,228 leads, $5.16 CPL) and 55–64 cohort (1,170 leads, $6.62 CPL) representing the highest-volume demographic segments in the account. The 35–44 cohort (1,888 leads, $5.05 CPL) also contributes substantially. This ICP skews older than the career-seeker and is the likely recipient of treatment-specific hooks (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES, PEPTIDE). Demographic data is account-level aggregate at 98.8% spend coverage — high confidence on the demographic distribution but not separable at the ICP level from the career-seeker without creative-level demographic breakdowns. Facebook Feed is the dominant delivery placement. The 65+ female segment (449 leads, $7.53 CPL) may represent this ICP's older tail but at lower efficiency.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Build Concept Column C2 of the next Matrix Sprint Test around this ICP using the STAT_ design system, treatment-specific hooks in each row (PERFECTPOUT Row A, FIXFROWNLINES Row B, PEPTIDE Row C, a new treatment hook Row D). Test without geographic qualifiers — the data strongly suggests geo-removal improves CPL for this ICP under broad Advantage+ delivery. Consider PR_VisualDemo (before/after treatment image) as the design constant for this column.

icp_profiles.profile_name: Healthcare or Wellness Professional Upskiller — The Clinical Credentialist
icp_profiles.message_resonance: Hypothesized resonance (low confidence, exploratory) with: profession-specific hooks (Nurses, Dentists, clinicians), peer testimonial proof (PR_Testimonial from credentialed professionals), rational ROI framing (FW_FAB, TN_Rational), credibility-forward copy (PR_Expert), and real practitioner video (UGC-style or documentary). Weakest fit with: consumer aesthetic outcome hooks (PERFECTPOUT, FIXFROWNLINES) and broad career-aspiration copy without clinical specificity.
icp_profiles.behavioral_signals: Sydney Nurses 2.mp4: $2.58 CPL, 74 leads, 44.0% CVR — competitive performance for a video format, suggesting the nurse-specific framing improves CVR significantly vs. generic video ($8.85+ CPL). STAT_DENTISTPROFIT_03.jpg: $5.41 CPL, 19 leads, 38.8% CVR — thin data (19 leads), low confidence. STAT_SCO_ENROLL_2.png: $5.24 CPL, 28 leads, 41.8% CVR — professional enrollment framing. This ICP is at MOFU — already interested in training but needs proof of professional legitimacy and peer validation before committing to a form fill. Volume signals are thin across all identified ads; this profile is exploratory and requires dedicated creative testing to validate.
icp_profiles.funnel_entry_point: MOFU via profession-specific social proof or peer testimonial on Facebook Feed or Instagram Feed. May also enter via professional community targeting signals — though broad Advantage+ targeting means the creative content itself must do the ICP self-selection work.
icp_profiles.psychographic_profile: This ICP is an existing healthcare or wellness professional — likely a nurse, dental professional, or allied health worker — who is exploring aesthetic medicine as a career extension or pivot to increase income or gain new clinical skills. She is more credential-conscious and skeptical than the career-transitioning non-clinical ICP. She responds to proof of professional legitimacy (PR_Expert), peer social proof from similar professionals (PR_Testimonial from nurses/clinicians), and ROI-framed messaging (income uplift, patient volume, practice profit). She is AW_SolutionAware to AW_MostAware — she knows aesthetic training exists and is evaluating specific programs on credibility and practical outcomes. Her HP_ is HP_Confidence (will this be recognized professionally?) and HP_Time (can I fit this around clinical shifts?).
icp_profiles.demographic_foundation: Likely females 35–54 with a clinical or healthcare background (nurse, doctor, allied health) based on the presence of 'Sydney Nurses 2.mp4' ($2.58 CPL, 74 leads, 44.0% CVR) and 'STAT_DENTISTPROFIT_03.jpg' ($5.41 CPL, 19 leads, 38.8% CVR) in the ad rollup, as well as SCO (Scottsdale), PAD, and LIVEPAT ad tokens suggesting specific professional audience targeting. Gender skew is likely female based on the account's overall 80%+ female lead volume. This is an exploratory ICP — avatar_basis is exploratory — with no dedicated ICP column historical data. Confidence is low-to-validation_required. The Sydney Nurses ad suggests geographic expansion beyond the US may be tested or this is a separate market signal.
icp_profiles.strategic_recommendation: Assign Concept Column C3 of the next Matrix Sprint Test as an exploratory column for this ICP (avatar_basis: exploratory, target_icp blank). Test 4 creatives: Row A — nurse/clinical professional testimonial video (CN_Testimonial + PR_Testimonial), Row B — static image with profession-specific hook and ROI frame (FW_FAB + TN_Rational), Row C — founder or expert story about clinical credentialing (CN_FounderStory + PR_Expert), Row D — social proof image with clinical peer group framing (CN_SocialProof + PR_SocialProof). Treat all results as first-sprint directional data only — do not scale without 100+ leads per variant.

message_pillars.label: Feed-First Product Desire Loop
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Feed placements dominate both click and cart volume across devices. This pillar locks Feed as the primary creative canvas and tests concept angles that maximize thumb-stop and add-to-cart rate — the two most readable early signals available in this account.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Feed placements account for the majority of adds-to-cart in the dataset; the single highest-volume Feed row shows 22 link_clicks → 49 adds_to_cart (ATC rate >200% of clicks, indicating browse/scroll re-exposure), and a separate Feed row delivers 34 link_clicks → 14 ATC. Confirmed purchases on Feed: at least 1 attributed. Instagram Stories shows a strong outlier (2 link_clicks → 16 ATC → 5 checkouts → 1 purchase), suggesting high-intent micro-placement worth isolating. Facebook Reels and Threads each show 1 row with minimal volume — insufficient to action. Evidence is low-volume; treat as directional.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU awareness and ATC generation. Feed creative must earn the scroll-stop AND the cart tap in a single exposure. Stories variant acts as a MOFU retargeting complement.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Square/vertical 4:5 ratio optimised for Feed. Hero visual leads with the pet product in use (lifestyle moment). FAB copy structure: Feature → Advantage → Benefit in three text beats. CTA family: 'Shop Now' / 'See It In Action'. Distinct from Stories variant (9:16, shorter copy). Do NOT produce near-duplicate sizing — treat Feed and Stories as separate concept columns in the matrix.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements ON under Andromeda ABO structure. The Feed-dominant signal supports letting the algorithm allocate, but creative must be natively built for Feed first. Stories-specific creative isolated in its own matrix column so placement signal can be read separately.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Monitor ATC rate (adds_to_cart / link_clicks) as primary thumbstop proxy given purchase volume is too low for CPA verdict at this stage. Scale budget on cells where ATC rate exceeds account average once 50+ ATC events are logged per cell.

message_pillars.label: iPhone-Native UGC Social Proof Engine
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: iPhone is the dominant device across every funnel stage in the dataset. UGC-style creative natively matches iPhone consumption patterns and pairs with social proof messaging to reduce purchase friction — critical given the high checkout drop-off observed (many rows show 5–17 checkouts initiated with 0 confirmed purchases).
message_pillars.why_it_matters: iPhone rows account for 11 of 20 device-level rows. One iPhone row shows 17 link_clicks → 50 ATC → 17 checkouts → 1 purchase; another shows 11 link_clicks → 55 ATC → 11 checkouts → 1 purchase; another shows 18 link_clicks → 8 ATC → 8 checkouts → 1 purchase. Checkout-to-purchase conversion is extremely low across all rows (typically 1 purchase per 3–17 checkouts initiated), pointing to a confidence or trust gap at the final step. Android shows weaker ATC ratios. iPad rows are small-sample but show 2 of 3 confirmed purchases — noted but insufficient to action. All purchase counts are low; confidence is limited.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU trust-building targeting warm audiences and broad cold audiences simultaneously (Andromeda broad). The goal is to close the checkout → purchase gap by injecting peer proof before the final tap.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Raw-feel vertical video (9:16 and 4:5 cuts) shot on or styled as iPhone footage. Real or real-styled pet owner testimonial as hook. StoryBrand structure: character (pet owner) → problem (product search pain) → guide (SKOV Pet) → success (happy pet). On-screen text captions mandatory for silent autoplay. CTA family: 'Read Reviews' / 'See Why Pet Owners Love It' / 'Shop with Confidence'.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements. UGC format performs natively across Feed and Stories without manual placement forcing. Let algorithm route; measure ATC and checkout rate by placement post-hoc.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Track checkout initiation rate (checkouts / ATC) as the key mid-funnel metric. If UGC cells lift checkout rate vs. non-UGC cells by >20% at 30+ checkout events, prioritise budget shift. Do not declare winner on purchase count alone given current low volume.

message_pillars.label: Instagram-First Visual Desire Hook
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Instagram (Feed + Stories combined) carries the highest concentration of ATC events and all but one confirmed purchase in the platform-level data. This pillar tests visually-led, emotion-first angles optimised for Instagram's algorithmic content environment under broad Advantage+ targeting.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Instagram platform rows: one row shows 17 link_clicks → 42 ATC → 15 checkouts → 1 purchase; another shows 7 link_clicks → 51 ATC → 10 checkouts → 1 purchase; Instagram Stories row shows 2 link_clicks → 16 ATC → 5 checkouts → 1 purchase. Facebook Feed rows by comparison show higher link_clicks but lower ATC ratios (e.g. 17 clicks → 8 ATC, 15 clicks → 11 ATC, 13 clicks → 5 ATC). Instagram appears to generate disproportionate ATC per click. All numbers are low-volume; treat as directional signal only.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU cold audience entry via Instagram Feed and Stories. PAS framework surfaces the pet owner pain (problem hook) → agitates the emotional cost → pivots to SKOV Pet as the relief. Lifestyle visual does the stopping; copy closes the emotional loop.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: High-quality lifestyle imagery or short-form video (under 15s) showing pet + owner in aspirational but relatable home moment. Problem statement in first 2 seconds of video or as headline overlay on static. Aspect ratios: 4:5 for Feed, 9:16 for Stories — built separately, not cropped. CTA family: 'Discover the Difference' / 'Shop Now'. No heavy product spec copy — emotion drives the tap.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements with creative natively built for Instagram proportions. Facebook will receive creative via auto-placement but Instagram-native assets should be uploaded directly. Monitor platform-level ATC split post-launch.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Use Instagram ATC rate as the primary 72-hour signal. If Instagram cells sustain ATC/click ratio >2:1 (as seen in top rows), prioritise spend. Pause Facebook-only cells that show <0.5 ATC/click ratio after 500 impressions per cell.

message_pillars.label: Checkout Friction Eliminator — BOFU Confidence Close
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Exploratory expansion pillar. The account-wide data shows a systemic checkout abandonment pattern: across nearly every device and platform row, checkouts initiated dramatically outnumber purchases. This BOFU pillar is a transparent exploratory hypothesis — no historical creative data exists for it — designed to test direct confidence-removal messaging (guarantee, returns, trust signals) aimed at the abandonment moment.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Across 20 device rows: total checkouts initiated sum to approximately 78, total confirmed purchases sum to 5 — an implied checkout-to-purchase rate of ~6.4%. Across 20 platform rows: similar pattern. This is not a traffic problem; it is a conversion confidence problem. No existing creative data exists for BOFU-specific angles in this account. This column is EXPLORATORY (avatar_basis: exploratory, target_icp: blank). Numbers are attribution-window estimates; treat with caution.
message_pillars.funnel_application: BOFU warm retargeting of checkout-initiated non-purchasers and ATC non-converters. BAB structure: Before (stuck at checkout, unsure) → After (confident, pet thriving) → Bridge (SKOV Pet guarantee/proof removes the risk). Value stack communicates offer completeness: product + guarantee + support + fast shipping in one frame.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Static or short video (6–10s). Lead with risk-reversal headline: e.g. 'Not sure yet? Here's why 1,000+ pet owners chose SKOV' (copy must be grounded in real social proof before launch — do not fabricate numbers in live creative). Trust badges, return policy, and star rating visible. CTA family: 'Complete Your Order' / 'Get It Risk-Free'. This is an exploratory column — all four cells should vary angle variables broadly to discover what resonates before optimising.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements. For retargeting signal, use ABO with a separate warm-audience ad set if platform allows. Under pure Andromeda broad structure, this column acts as a BOFU signal test within the broad pool — watch checkout-to-purchase rate as the key metric.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: This is exploratory. Do not scale before seeing at least 10 purchases attributed across the column's cells. Primary early signal: checkout-to-purchase rate improvement vs. account baseline (~6.4%). If any cell reaches >15% checkout-to-purchase rate at 20+ checkout events, escalate to dedicated BOFU sprint.

active_hypotheses.label: Adding an explicit social proof hook (review count or star rating) in the first 2 seconds of Feed creative will increase add-to-cart rate compared to a benefit-led hook, because the checkout abandonment data suggests a trust deficit rather than a desire deficit.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 1 (Feed-First Product Desire Loop) — benefit hook baseline
active_hypotheses.risk: Low volume may prevent statistical separation before budget is exhausted. Social proof copy must be legally accurate — fabricated numbers invalidate the test and create compliance risk.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Feed creative with HK_SocialProof as the opening frame (e.g. '★★★★★ 500+ happy pets' overlay on frame 1) vs. control HK_Benefit opener
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_ variable: HK_SocialProof (test) vs. HK_Benefit (control). Distributed across matrix as: HK_SocialProof appears in cells C1B, C2C, C3A, C4D (one per column, different ICP/avatar each time, across varied FW_ and TN_ combinations). HK_Benefit appears in C1A, C2B, C3D, C4C. This gives 4 appearances each in distinct combinations, satisfying the 2–4 rule and enabling cross-avatar reading.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: HK_SocialProof cells achieve an add-to-cart rate (ATC / link_clicks) at least 25% higher than HK_Benefit cells at 40+ ATC events per group. Secondary: checkout initiation rate holds or improves.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium-high. The ATC data shows desire is present (high ATC/click ratios in top rows); trust signals at the hook stage may accelerate the funnel top and reduce checkout drop-off.

active_hypotheses.label: Instagram-native 9:16 Stories creative will outperform Facebook Feed creative on checkout initiation rate when the same copy and concept are run under Advantage+ auto-placements, because the platform-level data shows Instagram generating disproportionate ATC and purchase events per click.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 1 baseline — Feed 4:5 creative under auto-placements
active_hypotheses.risk: Advantage+ may not serve Stories-format creative predominantly to Stories placement, diluting the isolation. If platform delivery split shows <30% Instagram Stories delivery for C3, the test is inconclusive. Monitor placement delivery report weekly.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Identical concept and copy rebuilt natively in 9:16 Stories format (not cropped), isolated in its own matrix column (C3) so placement signal can be read per-column
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: CN_Design_* placement format: CN_Design_Feed4x5 (C1, C2 columns) vs. CN_Design_Stories9x16 (C3 column). This is a column-constant variable — all 4 cells in C3 share the Stories format while C1 and C2 share Feed format. Within each column, angle variables (FW_, TN_, HK_) rotate across rows A–D to prevent confounding.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C3 (Stories) column achieves checkout initiation rate (checkouts / ATC) at least 20% higher than C1 and C2 Feed columns at 30+ checkout events per column. Also monitor: ATC/click ratio and purchase count.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. The Stories outlier row (2 clicks → 16 ATC → 5 checkouts → 1 purchase) is a single data point — high-upside but low-confidence. This test converts that single signal into a structured hypothesis.

active_hypotheses.label: A PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solution) copy framework will outperform a FAB (Feature-Advantage-Benefit) framework on TOFU thumbstop and ATC rate for cold audiences, because Instagram's top-performing rows show high ATC from emotionally resonant exposures rather than feature-led ones.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 1 — FW_FAB baseline concept
active_hypotheses.risk: If the row-level creative execution quality varies (e.g. one cell has a weaker visual), the framework signal may be confounded. Enforce identical visual treatment across row A and row B, varying ONLY the copy framework.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Same creative concept and visual with copy rewritten in FW_PAS structure: open with a relatable pet owner pain (e.g. 'Still searching for a product your pet actually loves?'), agitate, then pivot to SKOV Pet as the relief
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: FW_ variable: FW_PAS (test) vs. FW_FAB (control). Distributed as: FW_PAS appears in row B across all 4 columns (C1B, C2B, C3B, C4B) — making it the row-B shared angle variable. FW_FAB appears in row A across all 4 columns (C1A, C2A, C3A, C4A). Each column varies avatar/ICP and design system, so the framework effect is readable across different audiences. This satisfies the row = ONE shared angle variable rule.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: FW_PAS row (row B) achieves a mean ATC/link_click ratio at least 20% higher than FW_FAB row (row A) at 50+ total ATC events across the row. Secondary: thumbstop rate (3-second video views / impressions) if video creative is used.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium-high. Pain-first angles are a foundational creative hypothesis for pet product categories where owner guilt and pet wellbeing are emotional levers. The account has no prior FW_ variable data to confirm, so this is a foundational isolation test.

active_hypotheses.label: A BOFU creative explicitly addressing checkout hesitation ('Not sure? Here's why pet owners trust SKOV') will lift checkout-to-purchase conversion rate above the observed account baseline of ~6.4%, because the funnel data shows checkouts vastly outnumbering purchases across every segment.
active_hypotheses.source: Account baseline: ~78 checkouts → 5 purchases (~6.4% checkout-to-purchase rate) across all current creative
active_hypotheses.risk: High. This is an exploratory column with no historical data. Under Andromeda broad targeting (no retargeting audience), BOFU creative may underperform because it speaks to a ready-to-buy intent state that broad cold audiences haven't reached. Purchase volume may remain too low for a verdict within a single sprint. Mark as low-confidence exploratory.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Pillar 4 (Checkout Friction Eliminator) column (C4) — four BOFU cells using FW_BAB + HP_Confidence + PR_Testimonial angle combinations, each varying TN_ and HK_ across rows A–D
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: ST_ variable: ST_BOFU (C4 column, all rows) vs. ST_TOFU/ST_MOFU (C1–C3 columns). The BOFU funnel stage is held constant across the entire C4 column while concept angle variables rotate across its four rows. This isolates whether BOFU-stage messaging structurally improves checkout conversion independent of specific angle execution.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C4 column achieves checkout-to-purchase rate >13% (2x account baseline) at minimum 20 checkout events across the column. If volume is insufficient within sprint window, use ATC-to-checkout rate as interim signal (target: >40% vs. observed ~25–35% in top rows).
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Potentially high strategic impact if checkout drop-off is confirmed as a trust issue. High uncertainty due to exploratory status and low purchase volume. Do not scale until 10+ purchases are logged in the column.

active_hypotheses.label: UGC-style creative (raw, phone-shot aesthetic) will outperform polished brand creative on add-to-cart rate across iPhone placements, because iPhone users in this account generate the highest ATC volume and UGC natively matches the content format they consume.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 1 — CN_ProductDemo polished creative baseline
active_hypotheses.risk: Creative production quality of UGC cells must be genuinely distinct from polished cells — if UGC cells are slightly cropped polished videos, the variable is not truly isolated. Requires dedicated UGC shoot or sourcing of authentic creator content.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: CN_UGC format column (C2) with raw-aesthetic video testimonial creative across rows A–D, varying FW_ and TN_ per row while holding CN_Design_UGC constant across the column
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: CN_Design_* column constant: CN_Design_UGC (C2) vs. CN_Design_Polished (C1). All other angle variables rotate identically across rows within each column. Post-launch, filter performance by device = iPhone to read the device-level signal. This is a column-constant isolation — the design system is the variable under test.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: C2 (UGC) column achieves ATC/link_click ratio at least 30% higher than C1 (polished) column at 60+ total ATC events across each column. Secondary: compare checkout initiation rate (checkouts/ATC) to assess whether UGC also improves mid-funnel trust.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: High. UGC is a well-established format for pet product categories and aligns with iPhone-native content consumption. The account's iPhone dominance (11/20 device rows) makes this a high-leverage test.

active_hypotheses.label: An aspirational tonality (TN_Aspirational — 'the pet life they deserve') will outperform a relatable tonality (TN_Relatable — 'we get how hard it is') on TOFU ATC rate for Instagram placements, testing whether aspiration or empathy is the stronger emotional lever for cold pet owner audiences.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 3 — TN_Relatable baseline (empathy-led copy)
active_hypotheses.risk: Low-to-medium. Tonality is a subtle variable and may not produce a separable signal at low spend volumes. Pet product audiences often respond to both levers depending on the specific pain moment. Consider this a hypothesis-generation test as much as a decision test.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Row C across all 4 columns shares TN_Aspirational as the single shared angle variable; Row D shares TN_Relatable. All other variables (FW_, HK_, CN_ format) vary within each row across the 4 columns.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: TN_ variable: TN_Aspirational (row C: C1C, C2C, C3C, C4C) vs. TN_Relatable (row D: C1D, C2D, C3D, C4D). Each tonality appears exactly 4 times across 4 different avatar/design contexts — satisfying the 2–4 distribution rule. The main diagonal (C1A, C2B, C3C, C4D) and counter diagonal (C1D, C2C, C3B, C4A) will carry cross-avatar tonality signals for highest-confidence reading.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: TN_Aspirational row (row C) achieves mean ATC/link_click ratio at least 20% above TN_Relatable row (row D) at 40+ total ATC events per row. If no significant difference, default to TN_Relatable for lower-cost production in next sprint.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. Establishes a foundational tonality direction for SKOV Pet creative DNA — high strategic value even if the quantitative lift is moderate.
